| [THEORY-078](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-078.md) v2 | Top Fisher eigenvalues span the class means | Papyan (2019), [LIT-619](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-619.md): for softmax cross-entropy the Gauss–Newton matrix G, which is the model's Fisher averaged over inputs, is an uncentred second moment of logit derivatives indexed by class and logit. It decomposes exactly into four terms (Eq. 28), and its top C eigenvalues match those of the class-mean term G₁. Papyan (2020), [LIT-613](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-613.md), splits those C into one global-mean outlier and C − 1 between-class ones, finds a C(C − 1) cross-class mini-bulk beneath them, and proves the whole pattern for a Gaussian toy model. Papyan (2018), [LIT-617](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-617.md), supplies the measurements and the attribution of the Hessian's outliers to G. The decomposition is algebra. That G₁ carries the outliers is measured, by eye, under a training protocol narrower than practice. So this is Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-083](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-083.md) v4 | Neural collapse forms, only partly on ImageNet | Papyan, Han & Donoho (2020), [LIT-618](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-618.md), measured 480 trained classifiers on seven datasets with VGG, ResNet and DenseNet. Through the terminal phase, within-class variability of last-layer features falls (NC1), and the centred class means become equinorm and equiangular with cosine −1/(C − 1) (NC2). The classifier aligns with them (NC3), and the decision becomes nearest class mean (NC4). They prove that NC1 and NC2 imply NC3 and NC4 for the MSE-optimal and max-margin classifiers, and that the simplex ETF is the unique error-exponent-optimal codebook. Read from the plots, collapse is close to complete on the four easier datasets and partial on ImageNet at the last epoch. Papyan (2020), [LIT-613](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-613.md), sees class means separate and grow more orthogonal with depth. The measurements cover one protocol, and the dynamics are unexplained outside free-features models. Within them, THEORY-278 (LIT-974) derives collapse for MSE under a re-whitened flow, and THEORY-286 (LIT-994) gives the cross-entropy endpoint under class imbalance. The paper's further claim, that the Hessian's class outliers are a symptom of collapse, is argued and not measured, and is left to [THEORY-078](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-078.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-086](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-086.md) v2 | NTK fits eigenspaces at eigenvalue-set rates | Three derived results that compose. Cao et al. Basri et al. (2019), [LIT-612](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-612.md): on uniform spherical data the Gram matrix is a convolution, so its eigenvectors are harmonics, with closed-form eigenvalues per frequency. The bias-free kernel is zero on odd frequencies k ≥ 3, and a bias restores them. Bietti & Bach (2021), [LIT-608](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-608.md), Corollary 3: the L-layer ReLU NTK decays as k^(−d) on S^(d−1), the same exponent at every depth. Active for the kernel regime on uniform spherical data, where every step is proved. It says nothing about networks whose kernel moves. | Active |

| [THEORY-111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md) v4 | Linear connectivity implies feature linearity | Zhou et al. (2023), [LIT-674](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-674.md): whenever two image classifiers are linearly mode connected, by spawning or by permutation, the features of nearly every layer of the interpolated network are proportional to the interpolation of the endpoints' features. This is layerwise linear feature connectivity, and two conditions, weak additivity of ReLU and a commutativity of weights with features, imply it exactly. Lubana et al.'s Lemma 2, [LIT-669](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-669.md), gives the exact one-hidden-layer case: linear connectivity between interpolating minima forces shared activation patterns, and with shared patterns the hidden features are linear along the path. Measured on pairs at three interpolation points, image classification only. The regularity outside image classification, and the step to many-model averages such as soups and SWA, are QUESTION-318. | Active |
| [THEORY-113](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-113.md) v2 | Merging disjoint-task ResNets trails the ensemble | Stoica et al. (2023), [LIT-665](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-665.md), merge ResNets trained from different initialisations on disjoint label sets. Permute-then-average fails, which they explain by the permuted model lying in a basin for its own task only. Mean cross-model feature correlation falls with depth (0.50, 0.37, 0.27 at three depths). Merging only the early layers and keeping later layers as task heads recovers most of the ensemble's accuracy. Merging features within one model as well as across both helps once the models are wide enough to hold redundant features. With full merging on ImageNet-1k, ZipIt! is no better than permutation (8.6%). No same-task control separates the effect of task difference from that of depth; that is QUESTION-316. | Active |
| [THEORY-116](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-116.md) v2 | Surviving barriers mark different mechanisms | Lubana et al. (2022), [LIT-669](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-669.md): models that rely on a synthetic cue and models that ignore it are separated by a linear barrier even after permutation matching. Fine-tuned models that keep a linear path to their parent keep its cue, and those that lose the path lose the cue. Their Conjecture 1 states this claim's direction. What their Appendix F.3 proves, for a one-hidden-layer ReLU network with interpolating minima, is the converse: linear connectivity forces identical activation patterns, so models relying on attributes of different complexity cannot be linearly connected under any permutation. Zhou et al. (2023), [LIT-674](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-674.md), support that converse in deep image classifiers, where linearly connected pairs have features that blend layer by layer. The stated direction rests on experiments with synthetic cues and on a one-layer sufficiency argument. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-117](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-117.md) v4 | Pair coverage, not data volume, drives composition | Uselis, Dittadi & Oh (2025), [LIT-667](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-667.md). In an n × n grid of two concepts with k combinations seen per value, ResNet-50s trained from scratch fit seen pairs and fail on unseen ones; four times the data of the same combinations leaves 60–80% drops, while more values and more combinations help. Features pass from spurious, to decodable but entangled, to linearly factored as coverage grows. Model selection was on the test set, by design, so the results bound what is possible. The record re-derived that exactly factored embeddings of every unseen pair are fixed by seen pairs connecting every value, as the paper's k = 2 cycle does. Honest selection, other architectures and more concepts are [QUESTION-207](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-207.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-169](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-169.md) v3 | In-context conditioning is training, in kind | Sun et al. (2024), [LIT-801](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-801.md), Theorems 1–2, with von Oswald et al. (2022), [LIT-792](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-792.md), Proposition 1. Linear attention equals a layer whose state is a linear model's weights, updated by batch gradient descent on the context from zero; softmax attention equals a Nadaraya–Watson learner whose "training" appends the context to a list; and, with constructed weights, one linear attention layer reproduces one gradient step of a linear regression on in-context pairs. These are identities of output for specific layers. They do not say that trained transformers do gradient descent (the anthology rejects that, [ANTH-THEORY-068](https://github.com/dmarx/anthology-of-the-sota/blob/main/record/theory.d/THEORY-068.md)), nor anything about weight updates that persist across sequences. | Active |
| [THEORY-175](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-175.md) v4 | Relative representations transfer only roughly | Moschella et al. (2022; ICLR 2023), [LIT-849](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-849.md), as read in [NOTE-652](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-652.md). The invariance is by construction; its class (the maps preserving each sample's cosines to the anchors, which include every orthogonal map times a positive scalar and every per-sample positive rescaling, but not translations) is the reader's statement, re-derived in a dated note. The approximate agreement is the paper's evidence: relative vectors match at cosine 0.86–0.97 across encoders, while ten-nearest-neighbour overlap is 0.10–0.39. It does not say the maps between trained spaces are isometries, which the source never measures ([QUESTION-211](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-211.md)), nor that the transfer needs no paired data: the anchors are paired data. | Active |
| [THEORY-176](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-176.md) v3 | Stitching penalty is not Blackwell's order | Bansal, Nakkiran & Barak (2021), [LIT-850](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-850.md), define the stitching penalty L_ℓ(r; A) − L(A), with L_ℓ(r; A) the least task loss of A's top layers fed r through a map from a simple family S, and use it to call one representation better than another. Read against Blackwell (1953), [LIT-781](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-781.md), and [THEORY-156](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-156.md), that ordering is one coordinate of the comparison of experiments with the decision rules cut down to A's head composed with S. It is not invariant under Blackwell equivalence, which the paper intends, and it meets Blackwell's order only where the fitted map reproduces the replaced layers exactly. The relations are this record's derivations from the paper's definitions, not the paper's. | Active |

| [THEORY-194](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-194.md) v6 | Mutual-information coarse-graining recovers RG | Koch-Janusz and Ringel (2017), [LIT-873](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-873.md): shown numerically on two 2D lattice models whose relevant variables were known (Ising block spins, dimer electric fields), with an iterated Ising flow giving T_c to about 1% and ν ≈ 1.0 ± 0.15, and analytically only for 1D and quasi-1D chains. The general equivalence of the objective with a short-ranged effective Hamiltonian is argued, not proved, and no system with unknown relevant variables was tried. | Active |
| [THEORY-195](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-195.md) v4 | Deep CNNs learn hierarchies via synonym invariance | Cagnetta, Petrini, Tomasini, Favero and Wyart (2023), [LIT-877](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-877.md): measured for depth-(L + 1) CNNs and deep fully connected networks on the Random Hierarchy Model with s = 2 and L ≤ 4, with a large-v scaling argument for the correlation threshold and an exact one-step-gradient model of a two-layer network on one patch. The law n_c m^L is fitted, not proved for trained deep networks, and in this model the correlation threshold and the grammar's size are the same expression, so the data cannot say which of the two sets it. | Active |
| [THEORY-196](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-196.md) v3 | Hyperbolic trees need bits linear in depth | Sala, De Sa, Gu and Ré (2018), [LIT-874](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-874.md). The upper bound is Sarkar's construction with the paper's bit count. The lower bound is proved for H² and one family of trees, with an approximation, and dimension's help is shown only as an upper bound. The cost is a cost of coordinates in a fixed-point model, not of the information in the tree, and it says nothing about Euclidean or linear-direction representations of the same hierarchy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-197](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-197.md) v4 | RBM training is RG only at a perfect fit | Mehta and Schwab (2014), [LIT-882](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-882.md), Eqs. 18–22: setting the RG kernel T = −E + H makes the RG coarse Hamiltonian equal the RBM's hidden-marginal Hamiltonian for every parameter value, and Kadanoff's exactness condition equal to zero KL divergence. Short of exactness the paper itself says the two use different variational schemes, and Koch-Janusz and Ringel ([LIT-873](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-873.md)) give a case where distribution fitting keeps the wrong variables. The free-energy part of the argument was derived independently here; Lin, Tegmark and Rolnick's v2 appendix makes it in substance (LIT-887). | Active |
| [THEORY-200](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-200.md) v2 | Deep nets gain synonym invariance as they learn | Tomasini and Wyart (2024), [LIT-880](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-880.md): measured for locally connected, convolutional and fully connected networks on the Sparse Random Hierarchy Model with s ≤ 3 and L ≤ 3, with thresholds for the two sensitivities tuned per setting; the sample size is about (s0 + 1)^L n_c m^L times s^(L/2) without weight sharing, with a one-step argument for the (s0 + 1)^L, and about (s0 + 1)^2 n_c m^L with it, unexplained. Both invariances keep the parent's label statistics by construction, so the model shows that trained networks do the grouping, not that the invariances could not separate, and the extension to images is an analogy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-201](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-201.md) v2 | Training size sets the depth of learned hierarchy | Cagnetta and Wyart (2024), [LIT-883](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-883.md), extending [LIT-877](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-877.md) from labels to masked tokens: the correlation plateaus and the noise floor are derived for the Random Hierarchy Model in the large-v, large-m limit; the loss steps and the representation probes are measured in small transformers and CNNs; the link between them is argued, not proved; and the real-text evidence, from two character-level corpora, tests the effective context window, not the hierarchy. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-202](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-202.md) v4 | Trace and partition conditions don't define RG | Lin and Tegmark (2016), [LIT-887](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-887.md), arXiv v1–v2 appendix, a part dropped from the journal text: a family of joint Hamiltonians with Z_tot = Z and the wrong marginal, and the remark that any non-interacting pair meets the trace condition. Under Mehta and Schwab's identification ([LIT-882](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-882.md)) the trace condition is a perfect fit of the data, so even an exact variational RG step leaves the coarse variables' meaning free. The restricted Boltzmann machine proper needs visible–visible terms for the second construction; that narrows the example, not the claim. Promoted on 2026-10-20 with both constructions re-derived. Whether the trace condition suffices inside Kadanoff's kernel families is QUESTION-205. | Active |
| [THEORY-212](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-212.md) v3 | Layer balance sets rich versus lazy learning | Dominé et al. (2025), [LIT-943](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-943.md), read in [NOTE-715](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-715.md). With whitened inputs and a λ-balanced start, W₂ᵀW₂ − W₁W₁ᵀ = λI, the full gradient flow is solved exactly. λ is conserved and sets the regime. As λ → 0, singular values are learned in sigmoidal stages, as in Saxe et al., and both layers become task-specific. As \|λ\| → ∞, learning is exponential, the NTK is static, and the larger layer stays near the identity while the smaller carries the task at scale ∝ 1/\|λ\|. The paper analyses gradient flow only. Under SGD the conserved quantity drifts ([THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md)), which [QUESTION-081](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-081.md) takes up. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-227](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-227.md) v3 | Mutual information doesn't fix representation | Tschannen, Djolonga, Rubenstein, Gelly & Lucic (2020), [LIT-247](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-247.md), read in [NOTE-749](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-749.md). Invertible RealNVP encoders on MNIST halves keep the true MI constant, yet trained with an MI estimator they gain linear-probe accuracy, and one trained adversarially against a linear probe ends "significantly worse than using raw pixels". At matched bound values the encoder architecture decides quality. What makes MI-trained representations good must therefore come from somewhere other than MI. The paper's alternative, that InfoNCE works as metric learning, is argued, not tested. | Active |
| [THEORY-228](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-228.md) v3 | Probe error bounded by augmentation conductance | HaoChen, Wei, Gaidon & Ma (2021), [LIT-249](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-249.md), read in [NOTE-740](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-740.md). On a finite augmentation space, with labels recoverable from augmentations up to error α and k ≥ 2r, every population minimizer of the spectral contrastive loss has linear-probe error Õ(α/ρ²_⌊k/2⌋), where ρ is the sparsest-partition conductance of the augmentation graph (Thm 3.8). The guarantee needs no conditional independence of the views given the label. It is a statement about the population optimum of one loss: it says nothing about what training reaches, nothing about InfoNCE, and its infinite-space extension is asserted, not proved. | Active |
| [THEORY-229](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-229.md) v4 | Barlow Twins learns eigenvectors in order | Simon et al. (2023), [LIT-242](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-242.md), read in [NOTE-741](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-741.md). For L = ‖C − I‖²_F with λ = 1, no batch norm and C symmetrized by hand, a linear model from aligned initialization learns mode j at τ_j ≈ −log(s_j(0)²γ_j)/(8γ_j) (Prop. 4.1, proved), the top spectral solutions are exactly the minimum-norm zero-loss ones (Prop. 4.3), and the kernel version is kernel PCA on K_Γ (Prop. 5.1). Generic small initialization is covered by an informal derivation only. The operator is built from the model's kernel and the sample pairs, not from the positive-pair density ratio, and the stepwise growth seen in ResNets under SimCLR and VICReg is an experiment, not a consequence. | Active |
| [THEORY-230](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-230.md) v3 | Fisher–Rao geometry agrees across LM families | Picozzi (2026), [LIT-936](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-936.md), read in [NOTE-755](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-755.md), a single-author v1 preprint with code on request. The matrix of Fisher–Rao distances between a model's next-token laws on a context battery is invariant to every output-preserving reparameterization, while activation geometry has a GL(d) gauge (Prop. 1); two models with identical outputs can have hidden geometries that rank-correlate at −4/17 (Prop. 3). Over ten transformer, state-space and recurrent models the mean rank agreement is 0.88 against 0.62 for mid-layer activations. Convergence is proved only as a consequence of each model's excess risk to a common law, and that bound is vacuous on real models. Against a law-matched null, about 9% of the top-six eigenvector overlap is shared beyond the laws. Promoted on 2026-10-20. Replication and a test that varies the law are QUESTION-216. | Active |
| [THEORY-233](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-233.md) v3 | CKA and Bures bound each other by rank only | Harvey, Larsen & Williams (2023), [LIT-250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-250.md), §5 and App. A.3, read in [NOTE-753](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-753.md). CKA = 1 − ½‖K_X/‖K_X‖_F − K_Y/‖K_Y‖_F‖²_F, while NBS = 1 − ½B²(K_X/Tr K_X, K_Y/Tr K_Y), with B the Bures distance. They induce the same topology, but CKA/√(r(K_X)r(K_Y)) ≤ NBS² ≤ min[r(K_X), r(K_Y)]·CKA, saturated at rank 1. NBS bounds CKA of the square-root kernels, with equality for commuting kernels. Linear kernels only, and the discrepancy is illustrated on Wishart samples, not trained networks. | Active |
| [THEORY-234](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-234.md) v3 | Equal LM laws fix embeddings up to linear maps | Marconato et al. (2024), [LIT-950](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-950.md), read in [NOTE-746](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-746.md). For p(y\|s) ∝ exp(f(s)ᵀg(y)) on a shared vocabulary, p_{f,g} = p_{f̃,g̃} iff the models are extended-linearly equivalent: invertible linear maps between the subspaces M and N that enter the logits, at any dimensions and without the diversity condition (Thm 5). The dimension of M is then a property of the distribution. Relational linearity, linear subspaces and linear probing hold in all equivalent models or none when Γ ⊆ N and Γ_q ⊆ M (Thm 14), and parallelism is shared only within N (Thm 15). Exact equality of distributions only, and no experiments. | Active |
| [THEORY-236](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-236.md) v3 | Linear-invariant similarity fails at full rank | Kornblith, Norouzi, Lee & Hinton (2019), [LIT-254](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-254.md), Theorem 1, read in [NOTE-743](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-743.md). If s(X, Z) = s(XA, Z) for every invertible A, and rank(X) = rank(Y) = n, then s(X, Z) = s(Y, Z): any two full-row-rank representations of the same n examples are related by an invertible linear map. So when width reaches the number of examples, an index with that invariance, such as CCA, says nothing. The theorem fixes no group; the paper's case for orthogonal invariance plus isotropic scaling is an argument from training dynamics, not a consequence of it. | Active |
| [THEORY-237](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-237.md) v3 | MI lower bounds relax one Barber–Agakov bound | Poole, Ozair, van den Oord, Alemi & Tucker (2019), [LIT-246](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-246.md), read in [NOTE-739](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-739.md). Writing q(x\|y) = p(x)e^f/Z(y) in Barber and Agakov's bound gives I_UBA, tight at f = log p(y\|x) + c(y). Jensen gives Donsker–Varadhan, a tangent bound on the log gives TUBA and NWJ (unique optimal critic 1 + log p(x\|y)/p(x)), and NWJ applied to a K-sample problem with the batch mean as normalizer gives InfoNCE. MINE's bias-corrected gradient is the exact gradient of TUBA. A Monte-Carlo DV estimate is neither an upper nor a lower bound. The InfoNCE optimum is cited, not derived, in the source (the record derives it, note of 2026-10-19), and the bias–variance comparisons are on toys. | Active |
| [THEORY-238](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-238.md) v4 | Encoder alone bounds generalization error | Sefidgaran, Zaidi & Krasnowski (2023), [LIT-245](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-245.md), read in [NOTE-742](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-742.md). Theorem 4: E[gen] ≤ inf 2√((2·MDL + K + 2)/n) + ε, where MDL is the expected KL of the joint law of the latents of the training set and an independent ghost set to any prior invariant under label-preserving permutations, and ε is the distortion allowed by lossy compression. It holds for any decoder. With a product prior it reduces to sample-wise mutual information. The bound is never evaluated, the prior may depend on unseen ghost data, and a 2√((K+2)/n) floor remains. It does not prove that I(X;U) cannot bound generalization. | Active |
| [THEORY-239](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-239.md) v3 | Top singular functions minimize probe error | Zhai (2025), [LIT-975](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-975.md), read in [NOTE-770](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-770.md): Lemma 1.4, Theorem 3.2 and Theorem 3.4 with App. B. The operator g ↦ E[g(A)\|X] runs from L²(P_A) to L²(P_X) and is never assumed self-adjoint; its singular value decomposition comes from composing it with its adjoint. The guarantee is for linear probes and approximation error at the population level only. The thesis never works a non-reversible kernel on one space; the note of 2026-10-19 works a three-state one. It says nothing of what a trained network reaches. | Active |
| [THEORY-241](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-241.md) | Same function, different internal decomposition | Kumar, Clune, Lehman & Stanley (2025), [LIT-944](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-944.md), read in [NOTE-771](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-771.md). For the skull, butterfly and apple CPPNs, SGD in the layerized evolved architecture fits the image, the network's whole function on the grid. It shows no reuse of the symmetric parts, and single-weight and random-direction sweeps distort the output, where the evolved networks' sweeps vary it meaningfully. Qualitative, curated and three images. The paper's account of why, the order of discovery in open-ended search, and its extension to large models are conjecture. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-243](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-243.md) v4 | Interchange interventions don't fix direction | Wu et al. (2024), [LIT-961](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-961.md), Appendix A, and Makelov et al. (2023), [LIT-968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-968.md), Appendix A.3 and §8, read in [NOTE-809](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-809.md) and [NOTE-782](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-782.md). Both rotate the same three-unit identity network. The input aligns with h₃ in one basis and with (h₁ + h₂)/√2 in the other, equally well under interchange interventions on the input (re-derived 2026-10-20). The reply says intervening on further variables separates them; that was not checked. Makelov et al. rest their verdict on component boundaries; the reply rests its on the interventions performed. Shown exactly for one constructed network only; whether trained networks have such ties is open (QUESTION-234). | Active |
| [THEORY-246](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-246.md) v3 | Class separation hurts linear transfer | Kornblith, Chen, Lee & Norouzi (2021), [LIT-1044](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1044.md), read in [NOTE-762](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-762.md). Across nine objectives for ResNet-50 on ImageNet, penultimate class separation R² runs from 0.349 (softmax) to 0.845 (squared error), Papyan's Tr(Σ_W Σ_B†)/C from 21.2 to 0.33, and mean linear transfer to eight new-class datasets falls with R² (Spearman ρ = −0.93), from 75.9% to 48.3%. Cosine-softmax temperature raises R² from 0.24 to 0.77 and lowers transfer from 76.0% to 58.9%. CKA puts the differences in the last third of the network; fine-tuning erases them. The cost is for new classes: relearning the training classes, more separation helps. Networks early-stopped near 92% training accuracy; one dataset; correlational across losses. Promoted 2026-10-20 on this one study (ADR-047 v3), narrowed to what it measured. | Active |
| [THEORY-251](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-251.md) | Few-shot failures arise at the readout | Kirsanov et al. (2025), [LIT-946](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-946.md), read in [NOTE-789](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-789.md): at five demonstrations, accuracy across draws of examples runs from below 0.1 to about 0.6 while final-layer manifold capacity barely moves, and consistently swapped labels fail while capacity matches gold labels. The readout explanation is inferred from that dissociation, not measured; base Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-2B, mostly synthetic data. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-256](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-256.md) v4 | Transformers embed factored states orthogonally | Shai et al. (2026), [LIT-986](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-986.md), read in [NOTE-758](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-758.md). The lossless embedding is an elementary theorem (Prop. 2.2, Thm 2.3, App. A). The rest is experiment on five synthetic factors: about 10 effective dimensions against 242 for the joint state, approximate orthogonality in the first two components, and under token noise a collapse to the factored form before expansion. It does not show that the preference is architectural rather than a feature of training, a question the paper leaves open, and it varies neither the objective nor the data domain. | Active |
| [THEORY-264](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-264.md) v2 | Demos and instructions use different heads | Davidson et al. (NeurIPS 2025), [LIT-942](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-942.md), read in [NOTE-803](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-803.md): 4 to 7 of the top 20 function-vector heads are shared between the two forms in twelve Llama and OLMo models, the two vectors add, and swapping heads and activations between them costs accuracy. Kirsanov et al. (2025), [LIT-946](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-946.md), read in [NOTE-789](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-789.md), find the same split in representational geometry. Neither shows that no common representation exists, only that these methods find none; neither varies a pragmatic frame. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-269](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-269.md) v3 | LRE causality tracks pretraining co-occurrence | Merullo, Smith, Wiegreffe and Elazar (2025), [LIT-972](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-972.md), read in full in [NOTE-786](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-786.md). 24 factual relations, three models, eight OLMo-7B checkpoints; r = 0.82 between LRE causality and mean subject–object co-occurrence, above either term's frequency alone. Correlational by the authors' own statement. The linear objects are per-relation affine maps between hidden states, not attribute directions. | Active |
| [THEORY-271](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-271.md) v3 | Parallelepipeds need equiprobable sentences | Torii, Maeda and Hidaka (2024), [LIT-977](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-977.md), Theorem 1 (§5.5), read in full in [NOTE-781](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-781.md). Necessity is sound and short. The case analysis over permutations, and sufficiency, are loosely written. Exact shapes, raw counts, one design, and independent aspects that make the concept lattice Boolean. It says nothing about the logarithm or PMI, about noisy or approximate shapes, or about attributes that imply one another. | Active |
| [THEORY-274](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-274.md) | Sequence models store graphs as geometry | Noroozizadeh, Nagarajan, Rosenfeld & Kumar (2025), [LIT-995](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-995.md), read in [NOTE-800](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-800.md). Empirical throughout: path-star graphs up to 5×10⁴ nodes, four tiny graphs, frozen-embedding controls; the two-layer spectral analysis is informal and rests on an unproved observation (App. F). It does not explain why deeper models prefer the geometry, which the paper poses as open, and its main transformer runs used weight decay. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-278](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-278.md) v5 | MSE training follows a central path to collapse | Han, Papyan & Donoho (2021), [LIT-974](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-974.md), read in [NOTE-783](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-783.md). MSE loss splits exactly into a least-squares term and a non-negative deviation term, and the deviation becomes negligible early in training in 15 dataset–network cells. On that central path, with λ = 0, the loss is ½ Σ 1/(ω_j² + C) in the singular values of Σ_W^(−1/2)M̃. Under a flow that re-whitens the features after every step, each ω_j grows as (4t/N)^(1/4), and their ratios tend to 1. That is NC1 and NC2, and NC3–NC4 follow. Not shown: that ordinary training is this flow, or anything for cross-entropy or with weight decay. | Active |
| [THEORY-279](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-279.md) v2 | Networks learn low-order statistics first | Belrose et al. (2024, ICML), [LIT-952](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-952.md), read in [NOTE-777](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-777.md). Over training, ConvNeXt V2, Swin V2 and RegNet-Y on five small image datasets are probed with images whose class means or covariances are grafted from another class, and with maximum-entropy samples that keep only those statistics. Accuracy on these rises and then falls, often below chance. Pythia fits unigram-sampled text before bigram-sampled text. The ordering is empirical and covers orders one and two. The Taylor argument that motivates it is a heuristic, and the paper does not measure an ordered sequence beyond second order. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-281](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-281.md) v3 | Perfect erasure caps kept information at H(X\|A) | Chowdhury et al. (2025), [LIT-963](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-963.md), read in full in [NOTE-820](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-820.md). The cap (Lemma 3.3) is a two-line chain-rule argument that needs only the Markov condition A → X → Z. The permutation condition is proved necessary and sufficient for deterministic maps (Appendices A.3 and A.4), with finite supports and disjoint groups. The paper's further statement, that the cap cannot be reached when the groups are not permutations, is false for stochastic maps, which reach it for any finite distributions with disjoint supports. | Active |
| [THEORY-282](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-282.md) v3 | Subspace interventions can fake localization | Makelov, Lange and Nanda (2023), [LIT-968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-968.md), read in [NOTE-782](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-782.md). Proved for the construction (§3.2, Lemma A.1); shown in GPT-2 Small's MLP8 on IOI (46.7% FLDD, falling to 13.5% without the null-space component, 4.2% interchange accuracy) and in GPT2-XL MLPs on factual recall, where a residual-stream direction passes the same test. It does not say that subspace patching is unreliable in general, nor that a found direction with a null-space component is spurious: in a one-dimensional readout the test passes both kinds. The reply ([LIT-961](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-961.md)) contests the label, not the measurements. | Active |
| [THEORY-283](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-283.md) v3 | Hierarchical features emerge one at a time | Defilippis, Krzakala, Loureiro and Maillard (2026), [LIT-940](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-940.md), read in [NOTE-805](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-805.md). Take x ~ N(0, I/d), n = αd, and f⋆ = Σ a_k g_k(⟨w_k, x⟩) with even links of generative exponent two and a_k ~ k^(−γ). Direction k is weakly recoverable at α_k = Θ(a_k^(−2)) (Thm. 3.2). The optimal weighted error is Θ(α^(−1+1/(2γ))) until α ≍ m⋆^(2γ). The spectral estimator on Σ T(y_i)x_ix_iᵀ attains both (Thm. 3.6). The cascade is in the number of samples, not in training time. The network result is for a spectral first layer plus a ridge readout, not gradient descent. | Active |
| [THEORY-284](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-284.md) v2 | Manifold paths recover feature metric to scale | Modell, Rubin-Delanchy & Whiteley (2025), [LIT-935](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-935.md), Theorem 1, read in [NOTE-802](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-802.md). Under Hypothesis 1 (continuous injective ϕ_f from a compact feature space to the sphere) and Hypothesis 2 (CosSim = g(d²) locally, g ∈ C², g′(0) < 0), path lengths scale by √(−2g′(0)). So geodesics on the representation measure the feature, without knowing g. Both hypotheses are assumed, not derived from training. GPT-2's years are homeomorphic to both a linear and a logarithmic scale, and only the metric test told them apart. | Active |
| [THEORY-286](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-286.md) v2 | Imbalance yields SELI, not simplex ETF | Thrampoulidis et al. (2022), [LIT-994](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-994.md), read in [NOTE-764](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-764.md). For the unconstrained-features max-margin problem under STEP imbalance, every solution has logits ŴᵀĤ = Ẑ (one-hot minus 1/k), ĤᵀĤ = UΛUᵀ and ŴᵀŴ = VΛVᵀ from Ẑ's SVD (Theorem 1). This is the ETF only if the data are balanced or binary. No finite ridge gives it under imbalance (Proposition 1), though the ridge path tends to it (Proposition 2). ResNet-18 and VGG-13 runs sit closer to SELI than to the ETF, and approach it more slowly at larger R. Not shown: that gradient descent reaches it, and anything with more than one seed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-287](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-287.md) | Located mediators predict OOD correctness | Huang, Tao, Icard, Yang and Potts (2025), [LIT-987](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-987.md), read in [NOTE-765](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-765.md). In Llama-3-8B-Instruct over five tasks and ten shifts, counterfactual simulation is best on 8 of 10; a probe of the located variable beats a probe of its orthogonal complement on 7 of 10. Interchange accuracy and predictive power rise together only until accuracy nears 1. It does not say that the located variables are constitutive, that causal features always win, or anything about shifts that change the mechanism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-288.md) v3 | Activation symmetry makes latents discrete | Bird (2025, v4 2026), [LIT-976](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-976.md), read in [NOTE-759](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-759.md). Autoencoders of width 12–32 and up to three hidden blocks on CIFAR and MNIST, with rotation-equivariant affine maps, initialisation and optimiser. Elementwise tanh (B_n) and Leaky-ReLU (S_n) give beams along or against the basis, or on the ±1 diagonal, and radial tanh and Leaky-ReLU (O(n)) do not. The evidence is density plots, five seeds a condition, with no statistic. The downstream claims, that this causes grandmother neurons, superposition and neural collapse, are untested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-292](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-292.md) | Concept-direction alignment is a fitting artefact | Erogullari, Lapuschkin, Samek and Pahde (2025), [LIT-937](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-937.md), read in full in [NOTE-816](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-816.md). Shown at the last convolutional layer of VGG16 and ResNet18 on CelebA (natural correlations) and FunnyBirds (an injected 70% beak–tail correlation). AUROC is "largely preserved" by the paper's account, with no values in the text and no error bars. It does not say the model's own axes are orthogonal, and it says nothing about attributes that imply one another. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-294](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-294.md) v4 | Lazy training leaves NC1 where it started | Kothapalli & Tirer (2024), [LIT-985](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-985.md), read in [NOTE-774](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-774.md). NC1 = tr Σ_W / tr Σ_B of kernel-defined features is a ratio of linear functionals of the kernel matrix (Theorem 4.1). For one-dimensional data, two classes on opposite sides of the origin and zero bias, the ReLU tangent kernel of a wide two-layer net is a constant multiple of the NNGP kernel, so NC1 is the same (Theorem 5.1, re-derived). In higher dimensions it is measured no lower, and for ReLU higher; whether lazy training leaves NC1 in place there is [QUESTION-192](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-192.md). The inference that collapse requires feature learning is the reading's, not proved. | Active |
| [THEORY-299](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-299.md) v3 | KG embeddings learn sheaf margins, not sections | Gebhart, Hansen and Schrater (2021; AISTATS 2023), [LIT-232](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-232.md), §4 and Appendices A and C, read in [NOTE-843](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-843.md). A direct identification, covering Structured Embedding, the Unstructured Model, TransE, TransR and RotatE and not bilinear models. That existence of a section is trivial here, and that the only gluing question is whether fixed data extend, is the paper's own remark taken further by the record; it is what separates this use of sheaves from the contextuality line. | Active |
| [THEORY-301](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-301.md) v2 | Small Procrustes forces small decoding distance | Harvey, Lipshutz & Williams (2024), [LIT-257](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-257.md), Proposition 3 and App. A.1, read in [NOTE-834](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-834.md). With K_X = XG(X)⁻¹Xᵀ/M, α = Tr K_X, β = Tr K_Y and R_Δ the participation ratio of K_X − K_Y, P⁴/R_Δ ≤ E‖Xw* − Yv*‖² ≤ (2(α + β)P² − P⁴)/R_Δ for targets with E[zzᵀ] = I. The Procrustes–Bures equivalence is imported from [LIT-250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-250.md). Kernels with orthogonal supports show the converse fails: Procrustes distance maximal, decoding distance as small as 2/r. Finite samples, linear readouts only. | Active |
| [THEORY-305](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-305.md) v2 | InfoNCE isn't spectral clustering proper | Tan, Zhang, Yang & Yuan (2023, ICLR 2024), [LIT-227](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-227.md), read in [NOTE-846](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-846.md): Theorem 3.1 and its proof (App. A), Lemma 2.5 and Definition 2.7. The identity between objectives is exact on a finite object set with symmetric π. The paper's "spectral clustering" is any Laplacian form plus any regularizer; it names no minimizer and no population optimum, so it supports neither an eigenvector reading of InfoNCE nor the density-ratio optimum of [THEORY-001](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-001.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-306](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-306.md) v4 | Small-batch class counts hurt joint-embedding SSL | Assran et al. (2022), [LIT-231](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-231.md), §§3–5 and Appendix C, read in [NOTE-850](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-850.md). The prior is explicit in MSN's loss (a KL to uniform over mean cluster assignments) and in SwAV's equipartition constraint. For VICReg it rests on an informal reduction of a simplified loss to K-means and on K-means's cited tendency to equal clusters, and for SimCLR on a cited equivalence, so the title claims the prior for MSN and SwAV only. The effect is shown with batches of two to eight ImageNet classes, one run per cell, not with natural long tails; the open half is QUESTION-171. | Active |
| [THEORY-312](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-312.md) v2 | InfoNCE upper-bounds a kernel dependence loss | Li, Pogodin, Sutherland & Gretton (2021), [LIT-248](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-248.md), eq. 28 and Theorem B.1, read in [NOTE-830](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-830.md). On a finite dataset of N images with one-hot identity labels, the large-batch InfoNCE loss equals −HSIC(Z,Y) + E_Z log E_Z′ exp(k − μ₁) exactly. The second term is nonnegative by Jensen (the record's step), and for a bounded kernel it is at least γHSIC(Z,Z) less a second-order remainder (Theorem B.1, printed with the remainder's sign reversed). It does not say InfoNCE is HSIC, and it says nothing of the finite-batch estimator. | Active |
| [THEORY-319](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-319.md) v3 | Contrastive ratio's linear readout nears Bayes | Tosh, Krishnamurthy & Hsu (2021), [LIT-251](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-251.md), read in [NOTE-841](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-841.md): Lemma 1, §2.3–2.4, Lemma 2 and Theorem 3. The label enters only through how redundant the views are about it; the representation is the density ratio p(x,z)/(p(x)p(z)), learned without labels. Population level. The error-propagation results need a uniform bound on the ratio, and the low-dimensional direct embeddings are shown to exist, not to be reached. | Active |
| [THEORY-320](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-320.md) v2 | Known classes steer which novel classes are found | Sun, Shi, Liang & Li (2023), [LIT-235](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-235.md), read in [NOTE-833](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-833.md). On the population graph, at the exact rank-k optimum, R(U*, y) = ‖(I − P_{L♭})U♭ᵀy‖² (Theorem 5.5, stated as ≤, proved as = in C.1). In a one-sample-per-kind toy, a known class sharing colour makes a colour labelling recoverable, and one sharing shape makes it worse than none (Lemma 5.4). The general error bound (Theorem 5.6) is approximate and pools all known classes into one block, and is not part of this account. Nothing here is about trained networks. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-420](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-420.md) | Rectangular weights' small singular values matter | Staats, Thamm & Rosenow (2024), [LIT-856](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-856.md), read in [NOTE-659](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-659.md). Freshly initialised matrices of BERT, Pythia and Llama follow the Marchenko–Pastur law; trained ones depart from it above the bulk, and, in rectangular matrices only, below it. Zeroing Llama-3 8B's smallest Down-Projection decile leaves 2.0% on GSM8K from 43.2%, worse than every decile but the largest, while the same decile of the square Attention-Output leaves 40.0%. Whether the below-bulk outliers are what carries the damage is not tested: the decile mixes them with the lower bulk, and overlap with the input's principal directions and ablation importance disagree for several matrix types. | Active |
| [THEORY-421](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-421.md) v3 | Hyperbolic radius only partly reads hierarchy | Yang, Zhou, Ying, Chen & King (2023), [LIT-871](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-871.md), read in [NOTE-669](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-669.md). Recentring on the centroid plus an outward push raises that to 75–84%. The diagnosis rests on one architecture, two synthetic trees and one table without variance, and the paper does not separate a real failure to order levels from the origin's arbitrariness under losses that see only pairwise distances. | Active |
| [THEORY-439](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-439.md) v4 | Test-time training beats in-context alone | Akyürek et al. (2024; ICML 2025), [LIT-796](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-796.md), read in [NOTE-637](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-637.md). On BIG-Bench Hard with Llama 3.1 8B and 10 demonstrations over five seeds, zero-shot 40.9%, in-context 50.5%, per-task LoRA test-time training then in-context 57.8%; 12 of 27 tasks gain at least 2 points, and Boolean expressions falls. Training the update on leave-one-out in-context tasks beats training on bare pairs (57.8% against 51.5%). The update is discarded after each task, so it is as transient as a context. It is two benchmarks and one model family, and which task property predicts the gain is open. | Active |
| [THEORY-445](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-445.md) | Group convolutions are equivariant by design | Cohen & Welling (2016), [LIT-314](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-314.md), read in [NOTE-288](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-288.md). G-correlation commutes with the left action of G by the change of variables h → uh (eq. 12), and so do pointwise nonlinearities and pooling over cosets, up to edge effects and for rotations that are symmetries of the grid. Matched-parameter p4 and p4m layers lowered rotated-MNIST error from 5.03% to 2.28% and plain-CIFAR10 error from 9.45% to 6.46%. The paper uses no irreducible representations, characters or Fourier analysis, learns nothing about which symmetry the data have, and does not separate the effect of equivariance from the changed channel structure. | Active |
| [THEORY-478](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-478.md) v3 | Diffusion hyperbolic distance keeps local tree | Lin, Coifman, Mishne & Talmon (2023), [LIT-870](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-870.md), read in [NOTE-675](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-675.md). The hyperbolic diffusion distance is equivalent to min{1, d_T^(2α)} for 0 < α < 1/2 (Proposition C.4), under heat-kernel bounds on the tree that are cited rather than proved; one Hölder step holds only for d_T ≥ 1, and repaired, the reader finds the admissible range halves. Pairs beyond a radius are only known to be far, which matches the method's best mean average precision and its higher distortion than hyperbolic MDS on five graph benchmarks. A Euclidean distance on the same multiscale features does far worse. | Active |
| [THEORY-481](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-481.md) v4 | Linear attention learns staged by input spectrum | Mainali & Teixeira (2025), [LIT-859](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-859.md), read in [NOTE-658](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-658.md). The prediction of one linear-attention layer reduces to p₂ W Σ̂_x q₁ x_q, a product of two learned factors, so averaged gradient flow decouples into modes with τ_α dp_α/dt = q_α(1 − p_α q_α s^∞_α) and τ_α = (ηP s_α²)⁻¹, logistic from a balanced start. The fixed point is ŷ = W Σ̂_x Σ_x⁻¹ x_q as N → ∞. The paper's finite-N form, the one Ahn et al. and Zhang, Frei & Bartlett found, holds at finite N only for isotropic inputs with equal modes. The trajectory is new. The decoupling into independent modes is exact as N → ∞. At finite N it holds only for isotropic inputs with equal modes: the paper commutes the non-diagonal empirical covariance at (A71) and (A73), and the correct Wishart moment couples the modes at order 1/N. Alignment of the weights with the data's eigenbasis is assumed throughout, the null blocks vanish only in expectation over tasks, and the transfer to non-linear transformers is timing coincidences. | Active |
| [THEORY-496](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-496.md) v2 | Demo label correctness barely matters in ICL | Min et al. (2022), [LIT-814](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-814.md), read in [NOTE-607](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-607.md). With k = 16 demonstrations, labels drawn at random from the correct label set cost 0–5 points against gold labels (2.6 on classification, 1.7 on multiple choice on average) across twelve model–inference combinations and 26 datasets. Out-of-distribution inputs, random English words as labels, or breaking the input–label pairing each cost far more. The random labels always come from the right label set, gaps reach about 14 points on single datasets, and the authors' reading that the models learn no new correspondence at test time is untested on tasks pretraining cannot have taught. | Active |
| [THEORY-503](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-503.md) | Truncated SVD is the best rank-r approximation | Eckart & Young (1936), [LIT-330](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-330.md), read in full in [NOTE-301](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-301.md), which checked the error bound. Only the Frobenius norm and real matrices are covered. Uniqueness is of the approximating matrix, under a spectral gap, never of the factors; the paper's last section argues the canonic components cannot be read straightforwardly as psychological factors. | Active |
| [THEORY-504](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-504.md) v3 | SAE fidelity measures disagree by site | Lieberum et al. (2024), [LIT-611](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-611.md), read in [NOTE-482](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-482.md). Across every layer and sublayer of Gemma 2 2B and 9B, JumpReLU autoencoders on the residual stream raise the language model's loss more, when spliced in, than MLP and attention autoencoders whose FVU is about the same; and autoencoders trained on the base model lose little loss on instruction-tuned rollouts while showing a larger FVU gap. The authors' explanations (the residual stream is the bottleneck; fine-tuning re-weights old features) are conjectures, and the authors say no agreed metric of autoencoder quality exists. | Active |
| [THEORY-565](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-565.md) v3 | Diffusion maps can recover Laplace–Beltrami | Coifman et al. (2005), [LIT-981](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-981.md), read in full in [NOTE-1441](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1441.md). The finite construction and its isometry are [THEORY-728](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-728.md); the paper's own diffusion distance is the one ã^(m) induces, not the inverse-stationary-weighted one. Theorem 2.1 and the α-family are stated without proof; the companion ([LIT-1246](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1246.md), [NOTE-985](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-985.md)) proves the α-family's limit, Active without boundary as [THEORY-744](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-744.md), and its heat-kernel step is [QUESTION-231](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-231.md). Self-adjointness comes from the kernel's symmetry, and "directed diffusion" is anisotropic, not a non-reversible chain. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-566](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-566.md) v3 | Hyperbolic nets curve only through biases | Ganea, Bécigneul & Hofmann (2018), [LIT-879](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-879.md), read in [NOTE-686](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-686.md), which checked the closed forms numerically. Möbius layers are defined as exp₀ ∘ f ∘ log₀, so any composition of them is exp₀ ∘ (the Euclidean composition) ∘ log₀, as the paper notes; only the Möbius bias, which is parallel transport from the origin followed by the exponential map, and the hyperbolic logistic regression's distances to geodesic hyperplanes are not absorbed by the chart. The structural fact is proved; that the networks' gains, confined to a synthetic task and to separating WordNet subtrees in low-dimensional Poincaré embeddings, come from those two operations is this record's inference. [NOTE-686](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-686.md) filed no THEORY. | Active |
| [THEORY-640](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-640.md) | Cross-modal representation convergence is weak | Huh, Cheung, Wang & Isola (2024), [LIT-302](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-302.md), read in [NOTE-286](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-286.md). The cross-modal score "only reaches 0.16" of 1, is maximised over layer pairs, and the metric was chosen after CKA "revealed a very weak trend". It is local neighbourhood agreement that rises with competence, not kernel equality and not convergence to a model of reality. | Active |
| [THEORY-683](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-683.md) | Example order swings few-shot accuracy widely | Lu et al. All 24 orders of four balanced SST-2 examples give accuracies from about 50% to above 85%, in GPT-2 and GPT-3 models of eight sizes; Spearman correlations of order accuracy between sizes lie between −0.35 and 0.27 (175B against 2.7B: 0.05). | [THEORY-698](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-698.md) v2 | Probe lattices are guaranteed by construction | Xiong (2026), [LIT-267](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-267.md), read in [NOTE-240](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-240.md). Theorem 1 is the basic theorem of formal concept analysis applied to the crisp relation got by thresholding Fisher-LDA probes, and it holds for every binary relation; the paper's own proof plan says so. The empirical content is that the thresholded probes on three 7–8B models agree with a GPT-4o-annotated incidence at macro F1 69.7–83.2 and predict WordNet subsumption at F1 57.1–77.1. No closure, absorption or recovered-lattice comparison is tested, and the paper's join is not a lattice join as written. | [THEORY-719](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-719.md) v2 | Two contrastive losses share a density-ratio min | Johnson, El Hanchi & Maddison (2023), [LIT-258](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-258.md), App. B.2–B.3, read in [NOTE-751](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-751.md): on a finite augmentation space, with every function of the two views allowed, the spectral contrastive loss is minimized by K⁺ = p⁺/(p⊗p) exactly, and the NT-Logistic loss with equal positive and negative classes by the log-odds log K⁺, so its exponentiated score is K⁺. Population optima over unconstrained functions only; not what an encoder reaches, and not InfoNCE, which is [THEORY-001](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-001.md)'s open part. | Active |
| [THEORY-723](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-723.md) | Softmax fixes representations up to linear map | Nielsen et al. (2025), [LIT-253](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-253.md), read in full in [NOTE-738](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-738.md), with Harvey, Larsen & Williams (2023), [LIT-250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-250.md), for the kernel side. What is observed fixes a representation only up to that observation's symmetry group: a centred linear kernel up to a translation and an orthogonal map ([THEORY-004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md)), and a softmax output distribution up to an invertible linear map of the embedding with the inverse transpose on the unembedding (Thm 2.2). KL can go to zero while the embeddings stay non-linearly related (Thm 3.1, Cor. 3.2), but d_LLV ≤ ε gives d_f,g ≤ 2Mε (Thm 4.7). Final layer only. It does not say what the Platonic hypothesis means; that is [THEORY-002](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-002.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-728](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-728.md) v2 | Finite diffusion maps preserve diffusion distance | Coifman et al. (2005), LIT-981, read in full in NOTE-1441, with the derivation written out here; the 1/π-weighted distance is the companion's (LIT-1246), not the paper's own. For n points and a symmetric affinity K with positive entries, A = D⁻¹K is a Markov matrix with stationary law π ∝ d. It is conjugate to the symmetric D^(-1/2) K D^(-1/2), so its eigenvalues are real and in [−1, 1], and in [0, 1] when K is positive semi-definite. The map x ↦ (λ_j^m ψ_j(x))_{j≥1} turns the m-step diffusion distance, weighted by 1/π, into Euclidean distance exactly. Truncation gives a lower bound. It says nothing about the continuum limit, which is [THEORY-565](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-565.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-730](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-730.md) v2 | Lattice co-occurrence gives Fourier embeddings | Karkada, Korchinski, Nava, Wyart & Bahri (2026), [LIT-860](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-860.md), Propositions 1, 3 and 4 and Corollary 2, with the proofs in Appendix E followed in [NOTE-664](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-664.md). The result is conditional throughout. It concerns an idealised embedding with W Wᵀ = \|M*\| and d ≥ rank M*, not a trained one. It needs the positive and negative parts of M* to be translation invariant separately (Assumption B.1), not M* alone. It says nothing about whether any corpus or model satisfies these conditions, which is [THEORY-183](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-183.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-732](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-732.md) v2 | Layerwise linearity explains mode connectivity | Zhou et al. (2023), [LIT-674](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-674.md), read in [NOTE-512](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-512.md) with Appendix A's proofs checked: for an L-layer ReLU MLP on a finite dataset, weak additivity of ReLU over the two networks' pre-activations and the commutativity W_A H_B + W_B H_A = W_A H_A + W_B H_B at every layer make the interpolated network's features at every layer exactly the interpolation of the endpoints' features (Theorem 1). Output-layer linearity, at any positive scale, keeps the path's error within twice the endpoints' (Lemma 1). Lubana et al. (2022), [LIT-669](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-669.md), Lemma 2: for one hidden layer and interpolating minima, linear mode connectivity forces shared activation patterns, and with shared patterns the hidden features are linear along the path. It says nothing about when the conditions hold. That trained pairs satisfy them is [THEORY-111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md)'s empirical claim. | Active |
| [THEORY-734](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-734.md) v2 | Hyperbolic trees need many bits of precision | Sala, De Sa, Gu and Ré (2018), [LIT-874](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-874.md), Lemma D.1, read in [NOTE-679](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-679.md), with the proof redone here without the paper's small-angle approximation. Only the root's children are used to fix the embedding's scale c, and then the chains turn the scale into depth. Plane only, one family of trees, fixed-point coordinates in the Poincaré disk, deg_max ≥ 15 and ε ≤ 1. It says nothing about H^r for r > 2, or about whether any tree needs fewer bits under another number system. | Active |
| [THEORY-737](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-737.md) | Novel labels' residual is what known rows miss | Sun, Shi, Liang & Li (2023), [LIT-235](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-235.md), Theorem 5.5 with its proof in C.1, read in [NOTE-833](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-833.md). The paper states the identity as ≤, and its proof is a chain of equalities. Re-derived here in three steps from orthogonality and least squares. With the paper's Lemma 5.1 it bounds the novel labelling's 0–1 linear-probe error by twice this residual. It is about the exact rank-k factorization of a population graph, not about trained networks. | Active |
| [THEORY-738](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-738.md) v2 | Imbalanced max-margin optimum is simplex labels | Thrampoulidis, Kini, Vakilian and Behnia (2022), [LIT-994](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-994.md), Theorem 1 and Corollary 1.3, read in [NOTE-764](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-764.md) and re-derived here. By [THEORY-726](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-726.md) the problem is nuclear-norm minimisation of the logits under margin constraints. The polar factor of the simplex-encoded label matrix certifies it optimal, because under step imbalance its off-diagonal entries are negative. It does not say that gradient descent or trained networks reach this geometry, which is [THEORY-286](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-286.md)'s. | Active |
| [THEORY-739](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-739.md) v2 | word2vec proxy learns eigenvectors in sequence | Karkada, Simon, Bahri and DeWeese (2025), [LIT-855](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-855.md), Theorem 1 and Proposition 2, read in [NOTE-660](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-660.md) and re-derived here. The quartic proxy is a function of WWᵀ alone, so von Neumann's trace inequality gives its rank-d minimisers. Gradient flow from an aligned start keeps the eigenbasis and reduces each mode to a logistic equation. It does not say that word2vec, or the proxy from random initialisation, behaves this way; that is [THEORY-182](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-182.md)'s. | Active |
| [THEORY-740](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-740.md) v2 | Deep linear nets learn modes one at a time | Saxe, McClelland and Ganguli (2014, 2019), [LIT-864](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-864.md) and [LIT-862](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-862.md), read in [NOTE-667](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-667.md) and [NOTE-666](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-666.md), re-derived here.
