One weight matrix on the same data relaxes every mode exponentially on the one timescale τ. It does not say that random starts follow the solution, which is [THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md)'s. | Active |
| [THEORY-745](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-745.md) | Diffusion-map truncation error is absolute | Coifman and Lafon (2006), [LIT-1246](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1246.md), read in full in [NOTE-985](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-985.md). The identity D_t² = Σ λ_l^{2t}(ψ_l(x) − ψ_l(y))² is exact. The paper's Proposition 1 says the truncated map keeps it "up to relative accuracy δ". The true bound is absolute and can be large relative to D_t for nearby points. In the refinement sense, the diffusion-map family coarsens with t only through the threshold. Finite sets, counting measure and reversible walks only. It says nothing about the manifold limit or about non-reversible chains. | Active |
| [THEORY-746](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-746.md) | Slow feature analysis is an eigenproblem | Wiskott and Sejnowski (2002), [LIT-1249](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1249.md), read in full in [NOTE-971](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-971.md). Within the span of a fixed basis, the slowest decorrelated unit-variance outputs are the bottom generalized eigenvectors of the pencil (⟨ż̃ż̃ᵀ⟩, cov z̃), and each output's slowness is its eigenvalue. A consequence the paper does not draw: a stack of such stages whose function spaces contain their inputs is never faster at a higher stage, componentwise, on the training signal, so in this model "higher is slower" is imposed by the objective, weakly, and can stall. It is about the training signal and a fixed function space. It says nothing about test data, about a generative model, about invariance as opposed to slowness, or about learning dynamics. | Active |
| [THEORY-759](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-759.md) | Network fits low frequencies first regardless | Rahaman et al. (2019), [LIT-1261](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1261.md), Experiment 1, read in full in [NOTE-983](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-983.md). With equal amplitudes, and with amplitudes rising from 0.1 at 5 cycles to 1 at 50, the normalised fit \|f̃(k_i)\|/A_i reaches 1 at low frequency first. This is the reverse of the order by strength that [THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md) gives for a deep linear network. One architecture, one optimiser, a 1-D input, ten runs averaged. The paper's theory gives a bound on speed, not this order. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-775](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-775.md) | VAE slowness prior gives SFA only when whitened | Schüler and Wiskott (2025), [LIT-1296](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1296.md), read in full in [NOTE-1015](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1015.md). The ELBO of a dynamical VAE with prior N(z_{t−1}, I) and encoder N(g(x_t), I) is Σ E log p(x_t \| z_t) − ½Σ‖g(x_{t−1}) − g(x_t)‖² − (T − 1)d/2, an exact identity. For linear Gaussian encoder and decoder on whitened input, the maximizer spans the bottom eigenvectors of the difference covariance with eigenvalue μ < 1, each scaled by (μ^{−1/2} − 1)^{1/2} and then rotated arbitrarily. So it recovers SFA's slow span, cut at lag-one autocorrelation ½, not SFA's features. On raw input it trades variance against slowness. It says nothing about nonlinear encoders, about predictive sufficiency, or about Turner and Sahani's model. | Active |
| [THEORY-782](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-782.md) | Grokking onset: pairs fix the representation | Liu, Kitouni, Nolte, Michaud, Tegmark and Williams (2022), [LIT-858](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-858.md), read in [NOTE-662](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-662.md), with Power et al.'s critical fraction ([LIT-341](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-341.md)). The paper presents the critical training fraction as where the training set's equations fix the embedding. [THEORY-181](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-181.md) holds the theorem for the ideal model and the match at the one size measured, p = 10 with 1D embeddings. Held to addition: for S₃ the networks generalise beyond this mechanism. The multi-size test is [QUESTION-199](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-199.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-786](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-786.md) | Nets learn grammar when correlations beat noise | Cagnetta, Petrini, Tomasini, Favero and Wyart (2023), [LIT-877](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-877.md), propose that deep networks learn compositional data by detecting the correlations between input patches and the class, and that the sample complexity is where those correlations emerge from sampling noise. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-195](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-195.md), the measured law and the synonym-invariance it coincides with. This is the mechanism, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-788](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-788.md) | Training past zero error yields neural collapse | Papyan, Han and Donoho (2020), [LIT-618](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-618.md), title their paper on the "prevalence" of neural collapse and present it as a pervasive outcome of the terminal phase of training. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-083](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-083.md), only what their runs measured: three architectures with cross-entropy on seven balanced datasets without augmentation. This is the general law, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-789](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-789.md) | Max-information coarse-graining finds RG variables | Koch-Janusz and Ringel (2017), [LIT-873](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-873.md), propose that their mutual-information criterion finds a system's relevant degrees of freedom with no prior knowledge of them. What the record holds as shown, [THEORY-194](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-194.md), is that it recovered variables renormalization already uses, on 2D models whose answer was known. This is the general thesis that result was offered for, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-793](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-793.md) | Barlow Twins learns eigenvectors one at a time | Simon et al. (2023), [LIT-242](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-242.md), read in [NOTE-741](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-741.md). The stepwise dynamics, the minimum-norm end point and the kernel-PCA form are proved from aligned initialization, and that part is the Active [THEORY-229](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-229.md). Generic small initialization rests on the paper's Result 4.6, which its authors style a result and derive informally in App. C, with numerical checks at d = 3. This THEORY holds that generic case. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-794](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-794.md) | Compositional generalization needs diverse combos | Uselis, Dittadi & Oh (2025), [LIT-667](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-667.md), read in [NOTE-525](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-525.md). Their title and abstract present diversity of combinations, not data volume, as what drives compositional generalization in vision models. Their evidence is ResNet-50s trained from scratch on two-concept grids, with checkpoints chosen on the unseen pairs, and that measured part, with the factorization theorem, is the Active [THEORY-117](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-117.md). This THEORY holds the general causal claim. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-797](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-797.md) v2 | MSE nets reach collapse along the central path | Han, Papyan & Donoho (2021; ICLR 2022), [LIT-974](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-974.md), read in [NOTE-783](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-783.md). The paper's proposed explanation of neural collapse under MSE in real networks, filed apart from its measured central-path proximity and its derivation in a renormalized model ([THEORY-278](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-278.md)) under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. Renormalization is imposed, not measured, and every experiment used weight decay, which the derivation excludes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-798](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-798.md) | Encoders differ by an angle-preserving map | Moschella, Maiorca, Fumero, Norelli, Locatello & Rodolà (2022; ICLR 2023), [LIT-849](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-849.md), read in [NOTE-652](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-652.md). The hypothesis behind relative representations, filed apart from what their experiments measured ([THEORY-175](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-175.md)) under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. The source assumes it and tests it only through its consequences; it never fits a map between two spaces. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-802](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-802.md) v3 | Causal abstractions are fixed only up to basis | The general reading that [THEORY-243](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-243.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the three-unit network it proves (batch 062). Wu et al. (2024), [LIT-961](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-961.md), conjecture that complex models have "multiple distinct fully correct abstractions" and that the causal-abstraction framework cannot settle structural equivalence; Makelov et al. (2023), [LIT-968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-968.md), §8, grant that crossing component boundaries makes "illusory" tenuous, and answer by privileging components. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. Its only support is the constructed tie. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-805](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-805.md) | Volume-maximizing SSL's equal-cluster prior hurts | The general reading that [THEORY-306](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-306.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the explicit priors of MSN and SwAV and to one experiment with two to eight classes per batch (batch 033). Assran et al. (2022), [LIT-231](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-231.md), read in [NOTE-850](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-850.md), argue the prior for the whole class, VICReg through an informal reduction to K-means and SimCLR through a cited equivalence, and read it as the cause of the degradation reported on real long-tailed data. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-808](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-808.md) | Transformers learn factored belief subspaces | The general reading that [THEORY-256](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-256.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the five Mess3 and Bloch Walk factors and the 4-layer GPT-2-style models tested (batch 019). Shai et al. (2026), [LIT-986](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-986.md), read in [NOTE-758](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-758.md), present next-token training (the paper is titled “Transformers learn factored representations”) as yielding factored, orthogonal belief representations; [NOTE-758](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-758.md)'s claims C2 to C4 are each shown on one family of synthetic processes. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. It does not include the paper's inference that the preference is architectural (C5), which App. D.4 leaves open, or the claim that the factored form persists at convergence under strong noise, which Fig. 12 contradicts. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-813](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-813.md) v2 | Lazy training doesn't produce neural collapse | The general reading that [THEORY-294](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-294.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the one-dimensional, zero-bias, two-class case it proves. Kothapalli and Tirer (2024), [LIT-985](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-985.md), read in [NOTE-774](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-774.md), draw it as their conclusion: the lazy regime does not collapse anything, so the data-dependence of collapse has to come from a kernel that moves with the data. Beyond the solved case their support is simulation on two-class Gaussian data, where the NTK comes out less collapsed than the NNGP. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-825](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-825.md) | Hyperbolic embeddings don't put roots at origin | Yang, Zhou, Ying, Chen & King (2023), [LIT-871](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-871.md), read in [NOTE-669](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-669.md), assert for hyperbolic graph models in general what they measured for HGCN on two synthetic trees: the root is not innermost and radius reads level only partly. The general form was the lead clause of [THEORY-421](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-421.md) until that account was narrowed to the measurement on 2026-10-20 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4); it is filed here so that it stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-865](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-865.md) v2 | Verbalizable directions carry verbal report | Gurnee, Sofroniew et al. (2026), [LIT-1347](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1347.md), read in [NOTE-1069](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1069.md) (main text in full, appendices in part). It is the functional analogue of conscious access, in the access sense only, found in a transformer and tested by intervention. The sharp edge: one company's models studied by that company, a lens whose own statistics draw the layer band, a flexible/automatic split partly defined by the result, and an explicit refusal to say anything about phenomenal consciousness. | Active |
| [THEORY-869](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-869.md) v2 | Ablating J-space cuts experiential language | Gurnee, Sofroniew et al. (2026), [LIT-1347](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1347.md), §3.5.3 and §A.23, read in [NOTE-1069](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1069.md). The authors conclude that "the J-space supports the model's propensity to provide rich experiential reports, whether about itself or another entity". The sharp edge: the measure is a register of text graded by another model, on five or six prompts per condition, in one company's models; and the effect holds for reports about others, so it is not evidence of anything the self-reports are about. | Active |
| [THEORY-965](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-965.md) | SAE features are units the model computes with | Templeton et al. (2024), [LIT-1533](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1533.md), read in [NOTE-1178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1178.md), with Bricken et al. (2023), [LIT-1545](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1545.md), for the one-layer case. The thesis of both papers: features are the model's own units, shown by steering. The authors' own hedges: steering needs features clamped beyond their observed range; the reconstruction error rides along; "we haven't rigorously evaluated our features against other steering methods". The record holds a result against it for known causal variables ([THEORY-968](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-968.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-966](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-966.md) v2 | ACDC keeps one input of a redundant OR | Conmy et al. (2023), [LIT-1547](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1547.md), Appendix M, read in [NOTE-1170](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1170.md). For out = 1 − ReLU(1 − x − y) with x = y = 1, removing either input alone leaves the output at 1, so the first one visited is pruned and the second is then kept; visiting y first keeps x instead. It does not say how common redundant paths are in trained models, nor that any other method does better: HISP keeps neither input. | Active |
| [THEORY-967](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-967.md) | Attention heads are repurposed during training | Wang, Hoogland, van Wingerden, Furman and Murfet (2024), [LIT-1535](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1535.md), read in [NOTE-1188](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1188.md). "Heads 0:1, 0:4, 0:7 ultimately become the two previous-token heads and (layer 0) Dyck head respectively. However, these heads appear to start out as simple n-gram heads." Layer-0 multigram heads lose information about simple n-grams from stage LM3, as path patching and composition scores show them coming to feed layer-1 bracket-matching heads. The "ago" n-gram moves from head 0:0 to head 1:0. Whether the late roles are built from the early ones, or merely follow them in time, is not tested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-968](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-968.md) v2 | SAE features never beat raw dimensions on MIB | Mueller et al. (2025), [LIT-1550](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1550.md), read in [NOTE-1169](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1169.md). Unsupervised SAE features were worse units than neurons for known task variables across ARC, MCQA, two-digit addition and RAVEL. It does not say SAE features are never causal units: the comparison is on residual streams, under one selection method, with the base reconstruction error carried into every intervention, and the best method is supervised by the hypothesis it is scored against. | Active |
| [THEORY-970](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-970.md) v2 | ACDC recovers manual circuits on real tasks | Conmy et al. (2023), [LIT-1547](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1547.md), read in [NOTE-1170](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1170.md). Edge AUCs with corrupted activations and KL: Docstring 0.982, Greater-Than 0.853, IOI 0.869 for ACDC, against 0.805, 0.693, 0.789 for HISP and 0.937, 0.806, 0.823 for SP. It does not say ACDC finds the true circuit: the reported circuits are incomplete, the results depend on metric, ablation and parent order, and negative components are missed at sparse thresholds. | Active |
| [THEORY-971](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-971.md) | Additive units cannot detect a given sum | Ameisen et al. (2025), [LIT-1552](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1552.md), read in [NOTE-1185](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1185.md), re-derived here. It is why their addition graphs contain "lookup table" features between operand features and sum features. Whether a given unit in a trained model meets the premise is an empirical matter: attention patterns that depend on both operands, or any earlier nonlinearity that mixes them, break it, and that mixing is exactly the intermediate step the result says is required. | Active |
| [THEORY-973](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-973.md) v2 | Induction heads cause abrupt in-context learning | Olsson et al. (2022), [LIT-1538](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1538.md), read in [NOTE-1173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1173.md): Arguments 1–3 for the small attention-only series, with the smeared-key models. The score jumps from under 0.15 to about 0.4 nats in the window where induction heads form, pattern-preserving ablation of the induction heads removes nearly all of it to the end of training, and an architecture that lets one layer express induction moves the jump. It says nothing causal about models with MLPs or large models, and nothing about few-shot task learning, which the score does not measure. | Active |
| [THEORY-974](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-974.md) v2 | Transcoder feature edges are input-invariant | Dunefsky, Chlenski and Nanda (2024), [LIT-1554](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1554.md), read in [NOTE-1174](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1174.md), Eq. 7 and App. D.2–D.4, re-derived here. The weight factor is a weight of the replacement model, not of the original, and it is exact only for the replacement. It says nothing about why attention attends where it does, and "input-invariant" holds only up to a per-token LayerNorm scalar and only while the later feature is active. | Active |
| [THEORY-975](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-975.md) v2 | Head learning coefficients cluster by function | Wang, Hoogland, van Wingerden, Furman and Murfet (2024), [LIT-1535](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1535.md), read in [NOTE-1188](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1188.md): §4.1, Figs. 1–2 and 11, appendices B, F.5 and G. Per-head curves of how degenerate the loss is in that head's weights separate the heads by what they end up doing, and the separation is in the curves' shapes over training, not only their end values. It is one small model, cluster counts chosen by eye, and estimates whose ordering, not value, the authors trust. It does not show that the coefficient predicts a head's type before the type is visible. | Active |
| [THEORY-976](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-976.md) v3 | Bias features fire on Human/Assistant format | Lindsey et al. (2025), [LIT-1541](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1541.md), read in [NOTE-1181](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1181.md). A feature for a trained-in goal is active across the Assistant context, not only where the goal applies, and suppressing such features suppresses the behaviour. It is one model organism, built so that the goal has a name in its training documents; the authors do not claim their method would find a goal that has none. | Active |
| [THEORY-977](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-977.md) v2 | Two-layer induction heads compose via keys | Elhage et al. (2021), [LIT-1534](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1534.md), read in [NOTE-1189](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1189.md): Analyzing a Two-Layer Model, Induction Heads, Term Importance Analysis, and the Correction. Composition between heads was scored by a normalized Frobenius norm of matrix products, minus its value for random matrices. The heads it picked out attend to the token after the present token's previous occurrence and copy it, which is the minimal induction circuit the framework predicts from K-composition with a previous-token head. It is one model, with no seeds or training details reported, and says nothing about models with MLPs or about when the heads form. | Active |
| [THEORY-978](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-978.md) v3 | Causal scrubbing can't tell correlated features | Chan et al. (2022), [LIT-1549](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1549.md), read in [NOTE-1168](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1168.md). In the causal-scrubbing algorithm an interpretation node enters only through sample_agreeing_x, which draws a datum with an equal value of that node, so only the equivalence classes the node induces on the dataset matter. The authors say it themselves: the method "doesn't allow us to distinguish between two features that are perfectly correlated on our dataset". It does not say that a passing hypothesis is otherwise wrong, nor anything about features correlated only imperfectly. | Active |
| [THEORY-979](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-979.md) v2 | Replacement model makes attributions exact | Ameisen et al. (2025), [LIT-1552](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1552.md), read in [NOTE-1185](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1185.md): the local replacement model, the edge formula and the appendix on steering, re-derived here. It is a statement about what an attribution graph is exact for, not about the model: exactness holds at the unperturbed point only, the error terms are constants with no inputs, and the frozen attention patterns are the part of the computation the graph does not explain. | Active |
| [THEORY-980](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-980.md) v2 | IOI circuit faithful on average, not complete | Wang et al. (2022), [LIT-1540](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1540.md), read in [NOTE-1167](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1167.md): §§3–4 and the appendices. The circuit implements "identify the names, remove the duplicated one, output the rest" through duplicate-token, induction and previous-token heads, S-inhibition heads and name movers, with negative and backup name movers. The faithfulness, completeness and minimality tests are the paper's own. It says nothing beyond these templates and this model, it treats MLPs as given, and its greedy search is printed in a form that does not match its description. | Active |
| [THEORY-982](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-982.md) | Claude 3.5 Haiku plans ahead within a pass | Lindsey et al. (2025), [LIT-1541](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1541.md), read in [NOTE-1181](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1181.md): the introduction ("Claude 3.5 Haiku routinely uses multiple intermediate reasoning steps 'in its head'"; "It displays signs of forward planning") and the discussion's sections on plan formation and working backward from a goal. The case studies show each mechanism on chosen prompts, and the same article has a case without it: on a jailbreak the model "doesn't know what it plans to say until it actually says it". The authors report a satisfying graph for about a quarter of the prompts they try. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-983](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-983.md) v2 | Learned rotations beat axis-aligned alignments | Geiger, Wu, Potts, Icard & Goodman (2024), [LIT-1551](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1551.md), read in [NOTE-1192](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1192.md). Layer 1 of the equality network (1.00 with \|N\| = 16 and two 8-dimensional subspaces) and layer 9 of BERT's [CLS] vector (1.00 with two 256-dimensional subspaces). It does not say the networks implement the algorithms in any stronger sense than interchange accuracy on training pairs, nor that the learned subspaces are unique: every rotation within them gives the same interventions. | Active |
| [THEORY-984](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-984.md) | Haiku composes Dallas→Texas→Austin in two hops | Lindsey et al. (2025), [LIT-1541](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1541.md), read in [NOTE-1181](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1181.md). A two-hop intermediate, measured by intervention on one prompt. The evidence that counts is the change of output under the swaps; the graph itself is of the replacement model. It does not say how often the model reasons in two steps, nor that the shortcut path is weak. | Active |
| [THEORY-986](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-986.md) v2 | Similar features recur across networks | Olah et al. (2020), [LIT-1543](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1543.md), read in [NOTE-1182](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1182.md): Claim 3, the universality hypothesis. Curve detectors and high-low frequency detectors are reported in AlexNet, InceptionV1, VGG19 and ResNetV2-50, with InceptionV3, a Places365 model and conv nets trained from scratch named in the text. The authors: "the only evidence we can offer today is anecdotal". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-987](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-987.md) v2 | Activation poorly predicts SAE ablation effect | Templeton et al. (2024), [LIT-1533](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1533.md), read in [NOTE-1178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1178.md): Features as Computational Intermediates and the appendix on ablations and attributions. On "The capital of the state where Kobe Bryant played basketball is" (Sacramento against Albany), the five features with the largest ablation effect, Kobe Bryant, California, capital, Los Angeles and the Lakers, rank as low as 70th to 162nd by activation. It does not say how often this holds beyond the two prompts, and for other prompts the authors found no intermediate features at this layer. | Active |
| [THEORY-988](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-988.md) | Attention-only logits decompose into path terms | Elhage et al. (2021), [LIT-1534](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1534.md), read in [NOTE-1189](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1189.md). For a two-layer model, T = Id ⊗ W_U W_E + Σ_h A^h ⊗ W_U W^h_OV W_E + Σ_{h₂,h₁} A^{h₂}A^{h₁} ⊗ W_U W^{h₂}_OV W^{h₁}_OV W_E, with each A^h computed from the model's own run and then held fixed. It is an identity, not an approximation, and it is exact only under its conditions: no MLPs, no layer norm (which enters as a per-path rescaling), no biases, and attention frozen. It does not say the terms are small, interpretable or independent in what they compute. | Active |
| [THEORY-990](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-990.md) v2 | Induction heads drive most in-context learning | Olsson et al. (2022), [LIT-1538](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1538.md), read in [NOTE-1173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1173.md). The paper's thesis: circuits with the induction head's mechanism, matching "[A*][B*] … [A] → [B], where A* ≈ A and B* ≈ B are similar in some space", "implement most in-context learning in large models". For large models the authors grade their own evidence correlational (Argument 1), weakly interventional (Argument 2), plausibility (Argument 4) and analogy (Argument 6). Their strongest alternative is that other composition heads, formed in the same window, carry more of it above some size. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-991](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-991.md) v2 | SAE features beat neurons for interpretability | Bricken et al. (2023), [LIT-1545](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1545.md), read in [NOTE-1191](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1191.md): the detailed investigations, the global analysis and the appendices, for run A/1 of model A. Median rubric score 0 for neurons and 12 for feature intervals (one author, 162 units); held-out logit prediction 74% against 58%; the Arabic, DNA, base64 and Hebrew features have no matching neuron. It says nothing about deeper models or other sites, nothing about whether the model is "composed of" these features, and nothing about how features compare with neurons as carriers of a known causal variable. | Active |
| [THEORY-992](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-992.md) v2 | Feature existence tracks concept frequency | Templeton et al. (2024), [LIT-1533](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1533.md), read in [NOTE-1178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1178.md): Feature Completeness. 100–200 single-word concepts per category, presence of a feature judged from Sonnet's explanations of the top five features on a prompt naming the concept, by a human rater. The 34M dictionary (about 12 million live features) had features for about 60% of London boroughs, although the model names them all. It does not separate frequency in the model's training data from frequency in the autoencoder's, which the authors say are similar mixtures. | Active |
| [THEORY-994](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-994.md) v2 | Replacement model diverges over later layers | Ameisen et al. (2025), [LIT-1552](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1552.md), read in [NOTE-1185](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1185.md). It is the method's own measurement of where a circuit read off its stand-in stops being the model's: close for a layer, diverging with depth. It does not say how faithful the circuits of any case study are, which were chosen and validated separately, and it is measured on 18L, not on Claude 3.5 Haiku, where the companion's case studies were run. | Active |
| [THEORY-995](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-995.md) | Backup name movers arise from dropout | Wang et al. (2022), [LIT-1540](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1540.md), read in [NOTE-1167](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1167.md), §3.4: "We hypothesize that this compensation phenomenon is caused by the use of dropout during training. Thus, the model was optimized for robustness to dysfunctional parts." The compensation is real (a 5% loss of logit difference after knocking out the three name movers); the cause is not examined. Appendix F: "Both the reason and the mechanism of this compensation effect are still unclear." | Proposed |
| [THEORY-996](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-996.md) v3 | Attribution patching finds key nodes cheaply | Kramár, Lieberum, Shah & Nanda (2024), [LIT-1531](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1531.md), read in [NOTE-1190](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1190.md). Ground truth is each node's exact single-node noising effect on the clean prompt's negative log probability. Recomputing the softmax for queries and keys removes many misses; dropping one layer's gradient at a time helps on single prompt pairs but not on the distributions, where AtP with the softmax fix or plain AtP is cheapest. It says nothing about coarser nodes, other model families, effect magnitudes or false positives. | Active |
| [THEORY-997](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-997.md) | Fine-tuning rewires existing circuits | Wang et al. (2025), [LIT-1539](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1539.md), read in [NOTE-1183](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1183.md). Their EAP-IG circuits (top 5% of edges) change edges 2.8–4.3 times as much as nodes over LoRA fine-tuning on five arithmetic tasks. A record simulation shows that a fixed edge budget on a transformer-sized graph gives the same contrast when only edge-level noise is resampled, so the counts do not yet show reorganization. Fine-tuning only, one model for most results, arithmetic only. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-998](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-998.md) v3 | Mid-layer MLPs at the subject recall facts | Meng et al. (2022), [LIT-1536](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1536.md), read in [NOTE-1166](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1166.md): §§2–3, Tables 1 and 4, and Appendices A, B and E. Causal traces: ATE 18.6%; the mid-layer MLP effect at the last subject token peaks at AIE 6.6% against 1.6% for attention. CounterFact on GPT-2 XL: ROME's score 89.2 (efficacy 100.0, paraphrase 96.4, neighbourhood 75.4), next best 66.9. It does not say where facts are stored: a rank-one edit with the same output exists for any one-dimensional fact patch ([LIT-968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-968.md)). | Active |
| [THEORY-1000](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1000.md) v2 | Corrected attribution patching is a good prefilter | Kramár, Lieberum, Shah & Nanda (2024), [LIT-1531](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1531.md), read in [NOTE-1190](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1190.md). The measured case is four Pythia models, three prompt pairs and two small distributions. The paper's own diagnostic is what would let a single new setting be checked without exhaustive patching. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1001](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1001.md) | Circuits sharing units cooperate; rivals compete | Musat et al. (2026), [LIT-1530](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1530.md), read in [NOTE-1177](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1177.md). In projected SGD training of a three-layer single-head attention-only transformer on in-context bigrams, three induction circuits are possible, and the winner depends on initial strengths outside the winner itself. The authors explain the pattern by cooperation through a shared unit and competition for layers. The evidence is one scan over two initial strengths with every other coordinate zeroed, in projected training. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1002](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1002.md) v2 | DAS finds unimplemented algorithms in wide nets | Geiger, Wu, Potts, Icard & Goodman (2024), [LIT-1551](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1551.md), §4.4, read in [NOTE-1192](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1192.md). A random network cannot implement hierarchical equality, so any IIA above 0.5 is made by the search. At widths near the input's there is none; at 4,096 there are 14 points. It does not say DAS results on trained networks are artefacts: the trained equality network reached 1.00 at width 16, where the random one stayed at 0.50. | Active |
| [THEORY-1004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1004.md) | Agreement features shift from tokens to grammar | Bayazit, Mueller and Bosselut (2025, ACL 2026), [LIT-1555](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1555.md), read in [NOTE-1186](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1186.md). Crosscoders trained jointly on the middle layer of two or three checkpoints, with features scored by their relative indirect effect on agreement minimal pairs at each. The reconstruction quality (C1) and RelIE's agreement with single-feature ablations (C2) are measured; the trends in this title are read by the authors from annotated features. It describes; it does not predict later checkpoints, and it cannot tell a feature carried forward from one re-learned in the same direction. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1005](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1005.md) | Transcoders match SAEs on sparsity and clarity | Dunefsky, Chlenski and Nanda (2024), [LIT-1554](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1554.md), read in [NOTE-1174](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1174.md): §4, Table 1, Fig. 3 and Apps. E–F. It does not say transcoders are better than SAEs in general. The SAE learning rate was not tuned, all runs shared one seed and data order, one layer per model was measured, and on Gemma 2 2B Gemma Scope found transcoders worse than MLP-output SAEs at fixed L0 ([LIT-611](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-611.md), [NOTE-482](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-482.md)). | Active |
| [THEORY-1007](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1007.md) v2 | Feature circuits are small but lean on error nodes | Marks et al. (2025), [LIT-1532](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1532.md), read in [NOTE-1187](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1187.md): §§2–3.2, Figure 3 and Appendices A, B and H. Faithfulness is (m(C) − m(∅))/(m(M) − m(∅)) with nodes outside the circuit mean-ablated, scored on the latter two thirds of each circuit only. The features plus the dense error terms are a small circuit; the features by themselves are not. It says nothing about what the error terms hold, and it does not compare features with neurons on equal terms, which the authors say cannot be done. | Active |
| [THEORY-1011](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1011.md) v3 | Facts stored as mid-layer MLP key–values | Meng et al. (2022), [LIT-1536](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1536.md), read in [NOTE-1166](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1166.md), §2.3 and §3: "the localized factual association hypothesis". It localizes recall along three dimensions, "(i) in the MLP modules (ii) at specific middle layers (iii) and specifically at the processing of the subject's last token", and conjectures "that any fact could be equivalently stored in any one of the middle MLP layers". The support is causal tracing and the success of rank-one edits at the traced site. | Rejected — Hase et al. (LIT-1578, THEORY-1024) meet this entry's own refutation clause for its localization part, in GPT-J on 652 CounterFact facts. ROME rewrites a fact at over 96% at every layer but the last, and the per-fact tracing effect adds at most 3.2 points of R² to edit success. The conjecture that any middle layer could store a fact equally was split out to THEORY-1039 and stays Proposed |
| [THEORY-1013](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1013.md) v3 | Features and circuits are units of understanding | Olah et al. (2020), [LIT-1543](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1543.md), read in [NOTE-1182](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1182.md): Claims 1 and 2 of the essay. The evidence is a set of examples in InceptionV1 (curve, high-low frequency and dog head detectors; the curve, oriented dog head and car circuits), argued with feature visualization, dataset examples, synthetic stimuli, tuning curves and the weights. The essay names polysemantic neurons as the main obstacle. It gives no count of how much of a layer is understood. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1014](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1014.md) | One-mechanism behaviours run on several pathways | Marks et al. (2025), [LIT-1532](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1532.md), read in [NOTE-1187](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1187.md): §3.3, §5 and Appendix C. Agreement across a relative clause: subject-number features promote verb forms directly, and a second pathway carries the number to the clause's end through PP/RC boundary features. Cluster 475: one mechanism detects verbs and adjectives that take infinitival objects, another nominal objects before an object complement. Cluster 382: general succession features and token-specific induction features. "While the clusters … seem at first to each represent a single mechanism, circuit-level analysis reveals in both cases a union of distinct mechanisms." | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1016](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1016.md) v2 | SAE feature count is not well-posed | Bricken et al. (2023), [LIT-1545](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1545.md), read in [NOTE-1191](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1191.md), Feature Splitting and Discussion; and Templeton et al. (2024), [LIT-1533](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1533.md), read in [NOTE-1178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1178.md), for the same splitting at 1M, 4M and 34M features in a large model. In a one-layer model one base64 feature becomes three, then more; in Claude 3 Sonnet a San Francisco feature becomes two, then eleven. The authors offer two pictures, an idealized set seen at varying resolution and feature manifolds with no finite description; both deny that one width is the right one. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1017](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1017.md) | Haiku plans rhymes before writing the line | Lindsey et al. (2025), [LIT-1541](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1541.md), read in [NOTE-1181](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1181.md). A target word represented before the text that leads to it, and used causally: it is the case study's own measurement, on one couplet and a 25-poem injection test. It does not say how widespread planning is, the "about half" being a count without a stated sample, and one of the article's displayed "success cases" does not end in the injected word. | Active |
| [THEORY-1018](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1018.md) | Acrostic jailbreak isn't recognized until written | Lindsey et al. (2025), [LIT-1541](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1541.md), read in [NOTE-1181](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1181.md). On this prompt the model "doesn't know what it plans to say until it actually says it". It is one prompt, partly effective, and the decisive refusal mechanism runs through attention, which the graphs do not show: the injection that produced a refusal needed attention left unfrozen. | Active |
| [THEORY-1020](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1020.md) v2 | Standard induction circuit explains only 35% | Chan, Garriga-Alonso, Goldowsky-Dill, Greenblatt, Lin et al. (2022), [LIT-1579](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1579.md), read in [NOTE-1196](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1196.md). Percentages are of 0.053 nats, the loss the induction heads 1.5 and 1.6 contribute on next-token examples whose last token is on an induction-favouring whitelist, measured by causal scrubbing. The naive story's shortfall is mostly in the queries (51% alone) and keys (79%), not the values (90%). It does not say what fraction of the model's whole loss, or of its in-context learning, the circuit explains, nor anything about models with MLPs. | Active |
| [THEORY-1021](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1021.md) | Attribution patching fails on large, early patches | Nanda (2023), [LIT-1581](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1581.md), read in [NOTE-1201](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1201.md). The post's map of where the first-order estimate can be trusted. The record holds it from one task in the post, from the mathematics of the estimate ([THEORY-1023](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1023.md)), and in part from Kramár et al.'s test on Pythia ([THEORY-996](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-996.md)), which found misses behind saturated attention, as this predicts, and tested no residual-stream nodes. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1022](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1022.md) v2 | Curve units detect curves as such | Cammarata et al. (2020), [LIT-1575](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1575.md), read in [NOTE-1198](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1198.md). The article's four claims (causality, generality, purity, family) taken together, as the authors state them. Generality and the family are measured ([THEORY-1028](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1028.md)). Causality rests on feature visualization and attribution. Purity rests on feature visualization with a diversity term and activation-binned labels, while most of the unit's firings, and 45% of its contribution to expected value, are not shown to be curves. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1023](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1023.md) v2 | Attribution patching is a first-order estimate | Nanda (2023), [LIT-1581](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1581.md), read in [NOTE-1201](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1201.md): the estimate and its mathematical properties, not its accuracy in any model. The cost is fixed (about four forward passes for all patches), the estimate is linear and so additive, and its blind spots follow from linearity: saturation, interaction between features, and LayerNorm's scale invariance. | Active |
| [THEORY-1024](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1024.md) v2 | Causal tracing barely predicts editing success | Hase et al. (2023), [LIT-1578](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1578.md), read in [NOTE-1194](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1194.md): §§4–5, Tables 1–8 and Appendices A–C. For ROME at GPT-J's layer 6, ρ = −0.13 between rewrite score and tracing effect; R² 0.947 from the layer, 0.948 with tracing added. Over twenty method–objective pairs the largest gain is 0.032 (fine-tuning on five layers, Fact Forcing). It does not say that facts are stored nowhere in particular, nor that the layer does not matter: the layer explains most of the variance, and ROME is best on average at the layer tracing favours on average. | Active |
| [THEORY-1026](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1026.md) | Localizing a fact differs from editing it | Hase et al. (2023), [LIT-1578](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1578.md), read in [NOTE-1194](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1194.md), §6: "Causal Tracing answers a question about where factual information is carried in representations in a Transformer forward pass, and this question turns out to be a different question than the editing question of where is best to intervene"; and, for why edits work where facts are not traced, "Many layers could store a fact, and it happens that some do". The authors note that this would be surprising, since layers cannot be swapped freely. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1027](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1027.md) | SAEs add to black-box hidden-objective audits | Marks, Treutlein et al. (2025), [LIT-1584](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1584.md), read in [NOTE-1193](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1193.md): §§4–5 and Appendix F. In the blind game the fastest team used SAE features, but semantic search with its query finds the same documents. Post hoc and unblinded, SAE features surface RM-bias knowledge from bias demonstrations and from the Assistant token, where semantic search fails. The model's objective is named in its training data. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1028](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1028.md) v2 | mixed3b curve units are orientation-tuned | Cammarata et al. (2020), [LIT-1575](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1575.md), read in [NOTE-1198](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1198.md): the behaviour of the mixed3b curve family as measured by feature visualization, rotated dataset examples, synthetic curves and, for one unit, activation statistics and blind hand labels. It holds for the neuron basis of one model. It does not say how the units are computed, what their weak firings encode, or what fraction of the layer is understood. | Active |
| [THEORY-1029](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1029.md) v2 | Finer scrubbing gains reflect washout, not insight | Chan, Garriga-Alonso, Goldowsky-Dill, Greenblatt, Lin et al. (2022), [LIT-1580](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1580.md), read in [NOTE-1195](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1195.md). Hypothesis 3a resamples head 2.1's input separately at each of up to 40 positions and recovers 77% (loss 0.97 ± 0.06). Hypotheses 3c and 3d also split each position's input into terms drawn from different inputs, and recover 84% (0.69 ± 0.05) and 81% (0.81 ± 0.05). The authors call the two results not legitimate. It does not say how often this happens in other models, nor that the adversary they propose would remove it. | Active |
| [THEORY-1030](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1030.md) v2 | Feed-forward units are key–value memories | Geva et al. (2021), [LIT-1576](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1576.md), read in [NOTE-1200](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1200.md): "feed-forward layers in transformer-based language models operate as key-value memories, where each key correlates with textual patterns in the training examples, and each value induces a distribution over the output vocabulary", and "we thus expect our qualitative empirical observations to hold across diverse settings". Evidence in one model, correlational only. ROME's storage hypothesis ([THEORY-1011](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1011.md)) borrows the name and reads keys and values at another level. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1031](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1031.md) | Spread MLP edits insert 10,000 facts at once | Meng et al. (2022), [LIT-1582](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1582.md), read in [NOTE-1197](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1197.md): §§4–5, Tables 1 and 2, Appendices A, B and F. On 10,000 true zsRE facts in GPT-J, MEMIT scores 50.7 against FT-W 42.1, MEND 20.0 and ROME 2.6. At a handful of edits ROME generalizes a little better. It does not show where facts are stored: the layer range is chosen from traces averaged over facts, which do not predict per fact where an edit works ([THEORY-1024](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1024.md)). | Active |
| [THEORY-1032](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1032.md) v2 | RM-bias training generalizes to held-out biases | Marks, Treutlein et al. (2025), [LIT-1584](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1584.md), read in [NOTE-1193](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1193.md): §3 and Appendices B–C. The model organism behind [THEORY-976](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-976.md). Behaviours never demonstrated in post-training become more frequent, and the increase depends on the model having read that reward models prefer them. Rates are judged by a classifier. Haiku already shows the held-out behaviours at 17%, so what generalizes is an increase, not a new behaviour. | Active |
| [THEORY-1033](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1033.md) | FF keys show patterns; values rarely predict | Geva et al. (2021), [LIT-1576](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1576.md), read in [NOTE-1200](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1200.md): §§3–5. 160 keys annotated, one annotator each: every key had a pattern (3.6 on average), covering 65–80% of top prefixes. Agreement between value and key rises to about 3.5% by the top layers, against 0.0004% for a random token. It says nothing causal: no unit was ablated or edited, and the patterns were not compared with those of random directions. | Active |
| [THEORY-1035](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1035.md) | Polysemanticity is loss-optimal capacity sharing | Scherlis et al. (2022), [LIT-1625](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1625.md), read in [NOTE-1205](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1205.md). The paper's account of polysemanticity in general: capacity allocation at the loss optimum, driven by sparsity, with architecture deciding block size. The general first-order condition holds for any loss under two stated assumptions; its application to trained networks, and the role of architecture, rest on toy models only. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1036](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1036.md) | Kurtosis above 3 makes features share neurons | Scherlis et al. (2022), [LIT-1625](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1625.md), read in [NOTE-1205](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1205.md): the quadratic toy model of superposition solved in closed form. Its loss separates by feature through capacity, so the marginal value of capacity is −∂L/∂C_i = 2n_i²/C_i², and sparsity, through k, decides whether returns to capacity diminish. It is the model the causal scrubbing appendix's §6 analyses. It holds for this model and says nothing directly about trained networks. | Active |
| [THEORY-1038](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1038.md) | Hand-written curve circuit partly replaces units | Cammarata et al. (2021), [LIT-1629](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1629.md), read in [NOTE-1207](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1207.md): the three results of Curve Circuits that test its account of the mixed3b curve units, the echo edit, the hand-written reimplementation and the substitution. Only the last is a number, and a small one. It holds for one model's neuron basis and says nothing about weak firings or other families. | Active |
| [THEORY-1039](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1039.md) | Any middle MLP layer could store a fact | Meng et al. (2022), [LIT-1536](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1536.md), read in [NOTE-1166](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1166.md), §2.3: "we conjecture that any fact could be equivalently stored in any one of the middle MLP layers". It was one clause of [THEORY-1011](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1011.md), which is Rejected for its other part, the claim that the traced middle layers are where a fact is stored. Hase et al. (2023), [LIT-1578](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1578.md), read in [NOTE-1194](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1194.md), measure edits succeeding at nearly every layer of GPT-J whatever tracing says ([THEORY-1024](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1024.md)). That is what this conjecture predicts, but it is not evidence of storage, since an edit can work wherever a layer can write the needed output ([LIT-968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-968.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1040](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1040.md) | Early vision units form cross-model families | Olah et al. (2020), [LIT-1624](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1624.md), read in [NOTE-1206](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1206.md). The article's organizing hypothesis: early vision's units come in families, some of them real structure (said to be recoverable by factorizing weight matrices), and the families recur across models. The census ([THEORY-1042](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1042.md)) is by eye in one model; neither the factorization nor a second model's sorting is shown. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1042](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1042.md) | 37% of early-vision units sit in catch-alls | Olah et al. (2020), [LIT-1624](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1624.md), read in [NOTE-1206](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1206.md): the census of InceptionV1's early vision, counted. A complete partition of 1,056 units into 77 groups, by eye; 37% in groups the authors flag as uncertain or catch-all, by their own words. It is a denominator for the circuits claim that units are typically features ([THEORY-1013](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1013.md)), not a measure of how many units are understood. | Active |
| [THEORY-1045](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1045.md) | Factorial HMMs avoid flat-HMM overfitting | Ghahramani and Jordan (1997), [LIT-1628](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1628.md), read in [NOTE-1203](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1203.md). Four sizes, 15 random parameter sets each, 20 training and 20 test sequences of length 20, four-dimensional, C = 0.0025I, one run per set. In bits per observation over the true model, the K^M-state HMM's test excess is 2.29, 9.81, 11.57 and 175.35; the exact factorial HMM's 1.05, 1.26, 2.51 and 4.49; the structured approximation's 1.04, 0.90, 1.53 and 4.30. It is a result on small synthetic problems the model generated, not on real data or long sequences. | Active |
| [THEORY-1047](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1047.md) | Curve circuit is a readable, simple algorithm | Cammarata et al. (2021), [LIT-1629](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1629.md), read in [NOTE-1207](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1207.md). The article's account of how curve detectors are built, and its claim that the account is the circuit. The family structure and the echo edit are measured ([THEORY-1038](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1038.md)); that the description is complete, and that the reimplementation matches the natural units beyond strong cases, is shown by figures only. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1124](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1124.md) | Log co-occurrences act as Euclidean distances | Hashimoto, Alvarez-Melis and Jaakkola (2016), [LIT-1801](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1801.md), §3, read in [NOTE-1329](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1329.md). The correlation follows a normalization chosen to maximize it; the two nearest-neighbour statistics are necessary conditions, the corpora exceed the asymptotic centrality bound and pass only a non-asymptotic range, and the free-association data fail the reciprocity criterion the paper states. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1127](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1127.md) | CycleGAN hides photo detail in faint map signals | Chu, Zhmoginov and Sandler (2017), [LIT-1800](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1800.md), §§2–4, read in [NOTE-1346](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1346.md). One trained model on one dataset. The noise curve (Fig. 3, 50 photographs) is the only quantitative result; the hidden details, the composing edits and the attack are shown by examples. Proposed: an empirical finding about one model, said by the authors to recur on other datasets, not shown. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1128](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1128.md) | Log co-occurrence of walks recovers geodesics | Hashimoto, Alvarez-Melis and Jaakkola (2016), [LIT-1801](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1801.md), Lemma 1 and Corollary 6, read in [NOTE-1329](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1329.md). Proved from the convergence of graph random walks to a diffusion and Varadhan's small-time formula, with an open conjecture needed for directed graphs; checked numerically on an unweighted ε-ball walk. Active as a theorem about the toy model. The authors say the model is not a model of language, and nothing here shows real corpora satisfy it. | Active |
| [THEORY-1133](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1133.md) | GW identifies matches only up to automorphisms | Alvarez-Melis and Jaakkola (2018), [LIT-1818](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1818.md), use the GW objective (their eq. 8) for word translation and do not state its ambiguity; read in [NOTE-1336](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1336.md). The invariance follows in two lines from the objective's form and was checked numerically, including a symmetric tree on which a branch-swapping coupling costs exactly what the true one does. Active: elementary and checked. It does not say how large the symmetry group of real embedding spaces is, and exact symmetries are rare in noisy data; near-symmetries give near-ties instead. | Active |
| [THEORY-1135](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1135.md) | OT under a global linear map is a GW problem | Alvarez-Melis, Jegelka and Jaakkola (2019), [LIT-1805](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1805.md), Lemmas 4.1–4.3 with proofs in Appendix D; read in [NOTE-1333](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1333.md). Each step was checked numerically. Active: proved, and checked. The conditions matter. The p = 2 link to GW holds for the original transport problem only when the target is whitened and all vectors have equal norm, which the paper states in two separate places. Nothing here makes the chosen class the right one for given data, and nothing in it is local. | Active |
| [THEORY-1136](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1136.md) | Poincaré embeddings differ by more than isometry | Alvarez-Melis, Mroueh and Jaakkola (2020), [LIT-1808](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1808.md), §§5–7, Figs. 1–2, Tables 1–2; read in [NOTE-1323](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1323.md). Proposed: single runs, one embedding method for the matching experiments, and GW, the obvious isometry-free baseline, is not run. It does not say why seeds disagree (the paper conjectures negative sampling), nor that the matching preserves the hierarchy's direction, which it does not enforce. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1139](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1139.md) v2 | Learned sheaf maps top heterophilic benchmarks | Bodnar et al. The results are empirical: Table 1 on nine datasets of 183 to 18,717 nodes with ten fixed splits, baselines copied from earlier papers, spreads of one to nine points; and one synthetic bipartite experiment in which the learned maps are inspected. Active as a report (ADR-065); the paper's explanation of its accuracy, that the model learns the right geometry, is tested only on the synthetic case and is THEORY-1220, Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-1141](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1141.md) v2 | Sheaf class sets which labellings diffusion splits | Bodnar, Di Giovanni, Chamberlain, Liò and Bronstein (NeurIPS 2022), [LIT-1811](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1811.md), §3.2 and Appendix B, read in [NOTE-1332](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1332.md) from the arXiv preprint v4. Active as mathematics: each separation result has a proof, and Propositions 9, 10 and 13 were checked numerically. The paper says the orthogonal construction exists only at d = 2 and 4; it exists at d = 8 as well, by the Hurwitz–Radon theorem, and was built. The results are existential: the separating sheaf is defined from the class labels, so they say what a sheaf can do, not that one can be found without the labels. | Active |
| [THEORY-1143](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1143.md) | Round-trip agreement says nothing of fidelity | Chu, Zhmoginov and Sandler (2017), [LIT-1800](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1800.md), §2 and §5, read in [NOTE-1346](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1346.md). The authors argue it from the many photographs a single map stands for, and support it with [THEORY-1127](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1127.md)'s evidence on one model; they propose, and do not run, the test of adding capacity to the smaller domain. Proposed. It is the converse of the record's collapse case for [CLAIM-496](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-496.md): there routes agree because nothing travels, here because everything does, out of sight. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1145](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1145.md) | Unsupervised alignment needs near-isometric spaces | Søgaard, Ruder and Vulić (2018), [LIT-1819](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1819.md), read in [NOTE-1337](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1337.md), with the GW results of Alvarez-Melis and Jaakkola (2018), [LIT-1818](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1818.md), read in [NOTE-1336](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1336.md). Proposed: the evidence is single runs of one adversarial method, plus one GW table, and the authors themselves report that some seeds succeed where the method otherwise fails. What it does not support is a typological law about dependent marking, or the reading that a good fit establishes that the matched words mean the same. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1149](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1149.md) | Co-OT bounds GW, equal for squared distances | Redko, Vayer, Flamary and Courty (2020), [LIT-1804](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1804.md), Propositions 2–3, read in [NOTE-1335](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1335.md) from arXiv v3. Proved via Konno's theorem on concave quadratic programs and checked numerically, including strict inequality for non-Euclidean symmetric matrices. Active. It does not say COOT's two couplings coincide at every optimum, nor that either is unique. | Active |
| [THEORY-1155](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1155.md) | COOT plans fixed only up to joint symmetries | Redko, Vayer, Flamary and Courty (2020), [LIT-1804](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1804.md), Proposition 1, read in [NOTE-1335](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1335.md); the composition step is elementary and was checked by enumeration on small matrices, including a two-community block matrix with 32 tied optimal plan pairs. Active. It does not say real response matrices have exact symmetries; noisy ones give near-ties, which is the practical form of the threat. | Active |
| [THEORY-1185](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1185.md) | Merging fails on features without counterparts | The wide form [THEORY-113](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-113.md) held before the eleventh status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-113](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-113.md), Active, is its evidence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1187](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1187.md) | Low-loss paths interpolate every layer's features | The wide form [THEORY-111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md) held before the eleventh status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md), Active, is its evidence. | [THEORY-1224](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1224.md) | Ablating J-space mutes experiential register | The wide form of Gurnee, Sofroniew et al. The measure is a model-graded register on few prompts, in one company's models, with no register control and no blind human rating. | Proposed |

(2026), [LIT-1347](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1347.md), kept here when the status review of 2026-10-30 narrowed [THEORY-865](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-865.md) to what their experiments measured and promoted it ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1). The paper asserts that verbalizable representations form a global workspace in language models. Its tests are on four models of one family, by their makers, with a selectivity split partly defined by the result; no independent replication is reported. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1262](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1262.md) | Dropping MTP's target term from the trunk helps | Teoh (2026), [LIT-1896](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1896.md), §6 Figs. 3–4 and Tables 2–6; read in [NOTE-1470](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1470.md). Proposed: one run per scale, four scales, no seeds or variances, margins of one to two percent. It does not show that data-anchored correction is dispensable: the output head keeps it, and the paper attributes the explicit-KL variant's weaker head to its absence there. | Proposed |

Proposed: single training runs, Qwen3 only, the teacher's advantage measured at two of three scales, and a second candidate cause, per-entry clipping, left in every run. It does not show that the teacher's privileged knowledge is useless; it shows that it is hard to transmit where the student cannot see what it rests on. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1274](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1274.md) v2 | MTP gradient equals self-distillation plus NTP | Teoh (2026), [LIT-1896](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1896.md), eqs. 1–3 and Appendix B; read in [NOTE-1470](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1470.md) and checked by finite differences. Active: elementary and checked. It is a gradient identity, not a decomposition of the loss's value, and it does not by itself make the self-distillation a projection onto less information: in the DeepSeek-style heads of the paper's main results the student sees the same tokens as its teacher. | Active |

(2025), [LIT-1998](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1998.md), read in [NOTE-1524](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1524.md) (main text in full, appendices C.2, G.2 and M). Active as the reported measurements, with their sizes and scope: two models, three main traits, synthetic datasets and an LLM judge. It does not say that persona vectors are the mechanism of persona change, which the authors leave open, or that the method finds personas it was not told to look for. | Active |
| [THEORY-1330](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1330.md) v2 | Role space's main axis ends at the Assistant | Lu et al. (2026), [LIT-1991](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1991.md), main text read in [NOTE-1505](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1505.md). Active as the reported geometry, with its sizes: three open-weight models, judge-filtered role vectors at one layer, base-model evidence from one model's PCs and two models' steering. It does not say the Assistant is a single direction (the authors call the linear assumption "likely flawed"), nor that the axis's meaning beyond its ends is settled. | Active |
| [THEORY-1334](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1334.md) | Prompts and finetuning share persona directions | Chen et al. (2025), [LIT-1998](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1998.md), read in [NOTE-1524](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1524.md). The mediating reading is the authors' framing and PSM's use of the paper ([LIT-1952](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1952.md): training-time shifts "can be regarded as conditioning"). What the paper shows is correlation of shift with expression, and steering effects in both directions; that the regularizer against the shift fails, with the trait moving to other directions, counts against a single direction being the carrier. Proposed for that gap. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1339](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1339.md) v3 | Assistant-axis drift follows latest user message | Lu et al. (2026), [LIT-1991](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1991.md), read in [NOTE-1505](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1505.md). The figures are the paper's (§§4.1–4.2), from 100 synthetic conversations per domain with frontier models playing the user. Active as the reported measurements with their design. Whether the same holds with human users, and whether a per-turn model beats an episode-fixed persona, is QUESTION-443's. | Active |
| [THEORY-1342](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1342.md) | Selection and transport split only for fixed input | Vaswani et al. (2017), [LIT-1959](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1959.md), read in full in [NOTE-1501](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1501.md), eq. 1 and §3.2.2; the circuit vocabulary is Elhage et al.'s ([LIT-1534](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1534.md), [THEORY-988](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-988.md)). Active: it is the definition of the mechanism, checked against the equations. It does not say that heads are interpretable observers, which the paper supports only with visualizations, or that the separation survives composition across layers. | Active |
| [THEORY-1350](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1350.md) v2 | Post-training conditions a persona posterior | Marks, Lindsey and Olah (2026), [LIT-1952](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1952.md), read in full in [NOTE-1512](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1512.md). Active as a statement of what the model says and does not say, all of it in the text. It does not say that the model is true: the authors are "overall unsure how complete" it is, its evidence is surveyed rather than new, and its updating is offered as "can be viewed as", with the strict form said to be too strong. | Active |
| [THEORY-1353](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1353.md) | Circuits form when last parts align at once | Dong (2026), read in [NOTE-1540](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1540.md). One rate equation, sites × attempts × drive × e^(−βK) minus destruction, with K the missing parts. Forward, a capability ignites above a data-concentration floor that is a saddle–node; backward, plasticity loss is site depletion, silent in the loss and repaired by a query–key reset; and no native SGD knob is a temperature. Evidence: a toy grid, ablation on Pythia (32 of 32 cells below partial credit, 22 of 32 on the preregistered criterion) and six seeds for the reset. Proposed: single-author, unreplicated, mixing unproved. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-1672](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1672.md) | Agentic RL helps only with ample turn budgets | What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents? (Zhu, Jin, Tu, Men, Hao, Li, Liu, Zhao 2026), read in [NOTE-1769](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1769.md) (Read). The paper asks what multi-turn agentic RL (GRPO mainly, also PPO and GiGPO, on Qwen3-4B/8B) improves over its base model, on four interactive benchmarks (DeepCoder-MT, BFCL v3, InterCode-SQL, FrozenLake), using the two-dimensional metric Pass@(K, T) of Zhai et al. (2026; arXiv 2604.14877, held as [LIT-2441](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2441.md)). Across sampling breadth K, the RL model beats the base model at every k, so in multi-turn settings RL pushes success beyond the base model's empirical Pass@K boundary (unlike single-turn results). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1703](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1703.md) | RL expands agent boundary; SFT contracts it | Zhai, Yan, Shao and Wang's PASS@(k,T) ([LIT-2441](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2441.md), read in [NOTE-1749](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1749.md)). The distinction is definitional and holds whatever the experiment shows; the experiment is one model, one tool and differences of a few problems. Its stated monotonicity in T holds of a policy that ignores unused budget, and its own per-depth estimates are not monotone. Proposed on the experimental half. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1826](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1826.md) | Edit condition-number growth degrades models | Ma, Wang, Xu, Ling & Gu (2025), [LIT-2552](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2552.md), read in [NOTE-1910](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1910.md). The causal reading rests on a perturbation upper bound for a proxy quantity, on the rise of the condition number with edits, and on a correlation between that rise and the decline (C.5). The remedy's benefit is shown on three editors and three LLMs. The sharp edges: there is no intervention on the condition number at fixed update size; the bound's side conditions are not checked; and PRUNE does not provably bound the condition number. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1827](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1827.md) v2 | Linear guardedness iff class means are equal | Belrose, Schneider-Joseph, Ravfogel, Cotterell, Raff & Biderman (2023), [LIT-2551](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2551.md), read in [NOTE-1912](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1912.md). Theorems in population moments, and exact for the moments fitted. The sharp edges: the guarantee is linear only, and the authors conjecture that nonlinear erasure without damage is intractable in general; there is no finite-sample bound; and the oblique eraser can enlarge norms. | Active |
| [THEORY-1828](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1828.md) | Null-space misalignment breaks multi-domain edits | Liang, Lin, Huang, Wu, Li, Wang & Yan (2026), [LIT-2554](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2554.md), read in [NOTE-1911](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1911.md). The intersection bound is elementary linear algebra and holds; the claim that misalignment explains the collapse rests on results from one editor family, five to seven domains and three backbones, with conflict used as a surrogate for forgetting. The sharp edges: the Conflict Index is degenerate as defined at the paper's own sizes unless null spaces are thresholded, and the threshold is not given; and in the seven-task test, ordering by conflict does no better than the average random order, which weakens the link from measured conflict to forgetting. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1829](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1829.md) | Null-space projection sustains sequential edits | Fang, Jiang, Wang, Ma, Shi, Wang, He & Chua (2025), [LIT-2555](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2555.md), read in [NOTE-1908](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1908.md). Exact preservation holds for an exact null space; the method uses a thresholded one, so preservation is approximate and its size unmeasured. The sequential-editing results are strong on LLaMA3 and hold on GPT-J and GPT2-XL. The sharp edges: no measurement of leakage, no reported null-space dimension, specificity well below pre-edit, and a misstated "best baseline" comparison. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1832](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1832.md) | KV cache reuse erodes multi-turn steering | Kang, Liu, Ma, Huang, Tan & Jiang (2026), [LIT-2549](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2549.md), read in [NOTE-1905](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1905.md). A high-level algorithm abstracts a network when, under an alignment partitioning the network's variables into cells mapped onto the algorithm's variables, intervening and then translating commutes with translating and then intervening. This is tested by interchange interventions that patch in values from a source input, distributed ones in rotated coordinates, and scored by interchange intervention accuracy. Interventions are generalized to "interventionals" so distributed features can be targeted, and many interpretability methods are recast in these terms. Bardes, Ponce, LeCun (2021), ICLR 2022, arXiv 2105.04906. The loss has three terms on the embeddings: invariance (mean squared distance between two views), a hinge holding each variable's batch standard deviation above 1, and a penalty on off-diagonal covariances, the last two applied to each branch separately. In the ablation the invariance term alone collapses everything to one vector, covariance cannot stop it, and the variance term does (57.5%, and 68.6% with all three, at 100 epochs; 73.2% at 1000). The hinge must be on the standard deviation: on the variance, its gradient vanishes and the embeddings collapse. That bears on [LIT-228](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-228.md)'s Laplacian-eigenmaps reading, which assumes a squared variance term. Pythia is eight decoder-only language models, 70M to 12B parameters, each trained once on the Pile and once on a deduplicated Pile (about 1.5 epochs) in one fixed data order, with 154 public checkpoints per model (step 0, ten log-spaced early steps, every 1,000 steps to 143,000) and tools to reconstruct the batches seen up to each; one run per size, cosine learning-rate decay to a tenth of peak. They pre-train Llama-2 and OLMo-2 models (0.5B-4B, at 20 and 140 tokens per parameter) across AdamW weight decay values, then fine-tune on twelve tasks. Weight decay above the default 0.1 gives better fine-tuned performance even where it worsens pre-training loss (OLMo-2-1B at 140 tokens per parameter), so pre-training loss does not rank models by what they become. The loss standardizes each embedding unit over the batch and drives the cross- correlation matrix between two distorted views' embeddings toward the identity. The diagonal makes the embedding invariant to the distortions and the off-diagonal decorrelates its units. It avoids collapse without negatives, predictors, stop-gradients or large batches, keeps improving with very wide embeddings, and both terms are needed: in the ablation, the off-diagonal term alone gives 0.1% linear accuracy, the diagonal alone 57.3%, the full loss 71.4%. Here because A27 used it as a non-collapse mechanism ([CLAIM-481](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-481.md)'s note of 2026-11-19); [LIT-228](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-228.md) holds its CCA reading. | [THEORY-2021](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2021.md) | Travelling waves carry global shape information | From the reading of [LIT-2836](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2836.md) in [NOTE-2133](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2133.md). Jacobs, Budzinski, Muller, Ba and Keller (2025), arXiv 2502.06034. Recurrent networks with only local encoders and local recurrence learn to propagate travelling waves that bring whole-shape information to each pixel; reading each neuron's activity over time, rather than its last state, lets them segment images that need global context, beating feed-forward CNNs of matched receptive field and, on Multi-MNIST, U-Nets of similar size. The motivation is Kac's "hearing the shape of a drum", and a wave RNN reproduces square drums' fundamental frequencies; even an unbiased convolutional LSTM learns waves. Here because A15 of the exchange "Topological protection explained" listed it beside Keller et al. as a way learned systems carry information ([QUESTION-491](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-491.md)), and [LIT-647](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-647.md) mentions it.
