Lu and Kankanhalli (2026), arXiv 2610.12002. Five test-time-training methods become tools that produce reusable LoRA skills over a frozen backbone, and a policy trained by distillation and GRPO decides per query whether to answer directly, reuse a skill or build one, on utility gain minus a compute penalty. On a benchmark deliberately enriched for queries where adaptation helps, it raises Qwen2.5-7B's verified utility from 0.256 to 0.510, cuts adaptation compute by about 30% under a moderate penalty without losing utility, and amortizes skill construction through reuse (61 of 100 reuses help, 1 harms). Here because A58 cited it for learning when to update: its rule, build when gain amortized over expected reuse covers the compute, is [QUESTION-095](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-095.md)'s trade and [CLAIM-303](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-303.md)'s criterion for parameter skills. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2024](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2024.md) | Damage in training makes NCAs regenerate | From the reading of [LIT-2798](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2798.md) in [NOTE-2135](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2135.md). Mordvintsev, Randazzo, Niklasson and Levin (2020), Distill, DOI 10.23915/distill.00023, CC-BY. A continuous cellular automaton with a small learned update rule shared by all cells grows an emoji from one seed; trained only to grow, the patterns die out, overgrow or are only almost stable; trained from a pool of their own outputs, the target becomes an attractor that persists and often partly regenerates; trained with damage, the patterns regenerate robustly, even from damage not seen in training. Here because A15 of the exchange "Topological protection explained" used it to separate persistence from regeneration, held as [CLAIM-566](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-566.md): the three training regimes do separate growth, persistence and regeneration, though persistence training brings some regeneration with it, and the regenerating rule is supplied from outside the pattern. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2025](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2025.md) | MAML works by feature reuse, not adaptation | From the reading of [LIT-2822](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2822.md) in [NOTE-2131](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2131.md). Raghu, Raghu, Bengio and Vinyals (2019), arXiv 1909.09157, ICLR 2020. On standard few-shot benchmarks, freezing MAML's network body at test time barely changes accuracy, and body representations hardly move during adaptation (CCA above 0.9). MAML's success is therefore "feature reuse", not "rapid learning", and ANIL, which adapts only the head, matches MAML. It is here because A54 used it to separate reusable structure from the capacity to acquire structure, a clause of [CLAIM-758](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-758.md). The paper supports that distinction between routes to fast adaptation but does not measure acquisition capacity over training or forgetting. It also warns that a low adaptation budget can measure reuse rather than plasticity ([CASE-294](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-294.md)). Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2027](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2027.md) | Backprop loses plasticity over many tasks | From the reading of [LIT-2810](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2810.md) in [NOTE-2137](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2137.md). Dohare, Hernandez- Garcia, Rahman, Mahmood and Sutton (2023), arXiv 2306.13812 (v3, "Maintaining Plasticity in Deep Continual Learning"), published with Lan as "Loss of plasticity in deep continual learning", Nature 632, 768-774 (2024), open access. On long sequences of new tasks (Continual ImageNet, Permuted MNIST, class-incremental CIFAR-100, ant locomotion with PPO), standard deep learning gradually loses the ability to learn new tasks, which the authors keep distinct from forgetting. On ImageNet it falls to about a linear network, and on CIFAR-100 below retraining from scratch with old classes still trained. Small weights with continual injection of randomness (Shrink and Perturb, and their continual backpropagation) maintain plasticity, but all are applied from the start, and none is tested as a late rescue. It is here for overconsolidation (CLAIM-758) beside [THEORY-1353](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1353.md), whose depletion reading it fits: plasticity is lost while the network keeps practising on varied tasks. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-2033](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2033.md) | Contrastive loss splits into alignment, uniformity | From the reading of [LIT-2819](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2819.md) in [NOTE-2113](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2113.md). Wang, Isola (2020), ICML 2020 (PMLR 119), arXiv 2005.10242. As the number of negatives grows, the normalized InfoNCE loss on the unit hypersphere converges to an alignment term, minimized exactly when both members of every positive pair share a feature, plus a uniformity term, minimized by a uniform distribution of features on the sphere. On a finite augmented dataset the two optima cannot both be met, and weighting alignment far above uniformity maps every input to one vector. Across several hundred encoders, low alignment and uniformity losses go with good downstream accuracy, and optimizing them directly matches or beats the contrastive loss. Here because A27 used it for how self-supervised learning contracts some distinctions and keeps others ([CLAIM-481](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-481.md)'s note of 2026-11-19, [CLAIM-762](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-762.md)). It supports that split but is not spectral and says nothing of the classes kept. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2035](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2035.md) | Abstract rules follow data diversity, not design | Li and Webb ([LIT-2830](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2830.md)), read in [NOTE-2094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2094.md). The flip rate of a mean-difference rule vector is 0% at vocabulary 50, 5% at 100 and close to 100% from 500; at vocabulary 100 it goes from 5% with 2 rules to 95% with 10, and from 98% to near 0% as role-token bias rises, while every model still generalizes in distribution. At vocabularies of 100 or less the 12-layer model first solves the task without it and acquires it long after convergence. Ablated transformers and a pure MLP reach 90–100% at vocabulary 10k. The mechanism in the MLP is unidentified, and there is no random-network control. | Proposed |

Min, Lewis, Zettlemoyer and Hajishirzi (2021; arXiv 2110.15943, v2 May 2022) fine- tune GPT-2 Large on 142 NLP datasets presented as few-shot episodes, training it to predict the last example's output from the k before it. On 52 held-out target tasks, with no parameter updates, the meta-trained model beats plain in-context learning and multi-task zero-shot transfer in most of seven splits. The gains are largest on targets unlike the training tasks, and it matches a model 8x larger. Fine-tuning after meta-training remains better, and without meaningful label words every model falls near chance unless meta-trained on remapped labels. Here because A54 named it where meta-learning and in-context learning meet. It is the plainest case of outer training improving the interpreter so that it uses the signal better ([CLAIM-118](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-118.md)), and of the meta-learning arm of [CASE-294](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-294.md). | [THEORY-2039](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2039.md) | Task learning, not recognition, scales with size | From the reading of [LIT-2826](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2826.md) in [NOTE-2093](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2093.md). Pan, Gao, Chen and Chen (2023; arXiv 2305.09731) split in-context learning into task recognition and task learning. Recognition is measured with random labels from the correct label set, and learning with minimal prompts and a fresh mapping to abstract labels. Across 16 classification datasets and GPT-3, LLaMA and OPT from 350M to 175B, recognition is above chance at every size but flat in size and number of demonstrations. Learning appears only in large models and grows with demonstrations, matching gold labels with 16 examples in the largest. So Min et al.'s small gold–random gap ([THEORY-496](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-496.md)) widens with scale. Here because A56 proposed these controls for the in-context arm of [CASE-294](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-294.md), whose synthetic task families, with no pretrained prior, make in-context success task learning by construction. | [THEORY-2041](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2041.md) v2 | Trainable depth is set by a correlation scale | From the reading of [LIT-2825](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2825.md) in [NOTE-2101](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2101.md). Schoenholz, Gilmer, Ganguli and Sohl-Dickstein (2017), ICLR 2017, arXiv 1611.01232. In the mean-field theory of wide random networks with bounded activations, the correlation between two inputs decays to its limit over a depth scale ξc that diverges only at the order-to-chaos transition; gradients vanish or explode over the same scale on either side, and in experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 networks train only when their depth is below about 6ξc, so very deep networks train only near criticality, and dropout, which removes the transition, caps trainable depth. Here because A15 set it against domain walls as a way of keeping information through depth: it is the fine-tuned edge-of-chaos route that the read stand-in LIT- tmpyahtz ([THEORY-2051](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2051.md)) claims to avoid over a whole symmetry-broken phase. Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2042](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2042.md) | Function-vector heads drive few-shot ICL | From the reading of [LIT-2808](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2808.md) in [NOTE-2100](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2100.md). Yin and Steinhardt (2025; arXiv 2502.14010) compare induction heads and function-vector (FV) heads in twelve models (Pythia 70M–6.9B, GPT-2, Llama 2 7B). Ablating each type while sparing heads of the other shows that few-shot in-context accuracy depends mainly on FV heads, increasingly with scale. Induction heads matter for Olsson et al.'s token-loss difference, which the authors show measures something else. Across Pythia training, induction heads form near step 1,000 of 143,000. FV heads strengthen from about step 16,000 to the end, with few-shot accuracy, and many began as induction heads; that they are precursors is the authors' conjecture. Here because A56 used it for the in-context arm of CASE- tmphsr99. On Pythia it says in-context ability is still rising at late checkpoints, and it qualifies [THEORY-990](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-990.md). Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2047](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2047.md) | Laplacian eigenmaps minimize Dirichlet energy | From the reading of [LIT-2794](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2794.md) in [NOTE-2120](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2120.md). Belkin, Niyogi (2001), Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 14 (NIPS 2001), read from the proceedings PDF on papers.nips.cc. Laplacian eigenmaps embed the vertices of a heat-kernel-weighted neighbourhood graph by minimizing the Dirichlet energy Σ(y_i − y_j)²W_ij under yᵀDy = I and yᵀD1 = 0, which gives the eigenvectors of Ly = λDy with the smallest non-zero eigenvalues. The constraints are there because the energy alone collapses every vertex onto a constant, and each connected component is treated separately. The graph Laplacian is argued, heuristically, to approximate the Laplace-Beltrami operator. The authors speculate that the natural clusters it brings out might ground perceptual categories. Here because A27 grounded the owner's U12 connection, dissipation of differences as self-supervised learning, in it ([CLAIM-481](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-481.md)'s note of 2026-11-19; [LIT-228](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-228.md) holds the SSL equivalence). Keller, Muller, Sejnowski and Welling (2024), ICLR 2024, arXiv 2309.08045. A recurrent network whose recurrence is a ring convolution initialised as a one-step shift (the Wave-RNN) carries travelling waves in its hidden state, and against a matched wave-free network (the identity-initialised RNN) it learns faster and keeps inputs far longer: more than five orders of magnitude lower loss on the copy task, the adding task solved at length 1000, and much more input information retained with the recurrence frozen. The authors read the wave field as a register in which propagation stops later inputs overwriting earlier ones; randomly initialised local recurrences learn waves in training. A sliding-window Transformer keeps learning at test time by next-token prediction on its context, compressing it into the MLP weights of its last quarter of blocks, from an initialization meta-learned for the loss after those updates.
